memories.content: The /api/v1 mobile API authenticates with opaque bearer tokens stored hashed (sha256) in api_tokens, not JWT. Chosen so tokens can be revoked instantly by deleting the row and because the mobile app has no offline verification need. Tokens expire after 30 days idle; last_used_at is updated at most once per hour to avoid write amplification.

Concurrency in the executor: a tokio::sync::Semaphore with --jobs permits (default 16) wraps every transfer; multipart parts of one file share the file's permit plus a separate part semaphore (default 4 per file) so one huge file cannot starve small ones. Futures are driven with FuturesUnordered, not tokio::spawn per file, to keep borrow lifetimes simple and memory bounded.

Ignore rules: .fsyncignore files use gitignore syntax and are applied hierarchically by ignore::WalkBuilder with add_custom_ignore_filename(".fsyncignore"). .gitignore is honoured only with --respect-gitignore (off by default, because people sync build outputs on purpose). .ferrosync/ itself is always excluded.

Incident 2026-04-18: shopfront-worker-fulfillment pods were OOMKilled every few hours (limit 1Gi). Memory grew steadily per task because export_orders_to_kestrel loaded every order of the day with joinedload into one list and lxml kept the whole tree.

Fixes: worker_max_tasks_per_child=50 and worker_max_memory_per_child=700000 (KiB) in app/celery_config.py so children recycle; the export now streams with session.execute(select(...).execution_options(yield_per=500)) and writes the file incrementally. Memory per child now plateaus at ~260MB. Also learned: with prefork, the k8s memory limit applies to the parent plus all children, so concurrency 4 x 260MB plus parent must stay under the limit; fulfillment workers run with concurrency 2.

Deleting a product variant from the admin failed with "psycopg.errors.ForeignKeyViolation: update or delete on table "product_variants" violates foreign key constraint "order_items_variant_id_fkey"". Variants that were ever sold must not be deleted; the admin now only offers "deactivate" (is_active=false) when order_items reference the variant, and hard delete only for never-sold variants.

Certificate for shop.example.test stuck in Pending with the order showing "Waiting for DNS-01 challenge propagation: DNS record for "shop.example.test" not yet propagated". The hosted zone had a CNAME on _acme-challenge left from a previous provider, so the TXT record was never visible. Deleting the stale CNAME fixed it; cert issued within 2 minutes.

Monitoring: kube-prometheus-stack (Prometheus retention 15d, 100Gi gp3), Grafana with dashboards as code in k8s/platform/grafana-dashboards/*.json (loaded by sidecar via label grafana_dashboard=1), Alertmanager routing to the on-call webhook. Long-term metrics are not stored (no Thanos/Mimir) — a known gap. Loki 3 (single binary, S3 storage, 30d retention) for logs via promtail-less OTel collector daemonset.

First request to a bucket in eu-west-3 with profile region eu-central-1 failed with "PermanentRedirect: The bucket you are attempting to access must be addressed using the specified endpoint." We now call HeadBucket at startup, read the x-amz-bucket-region header from the 301 response and rebuild the client for that region, caching it in manifest meta.bucket_region.

User wants ruff for both linting and formatting (ruff format, line-length 100); black and isort were removed from pyproject.toml in April. Do not reintroduce them. Run `make lint` before proposing a commit.

Auth: email magic link + Sign in with Apple. Access token (15 min JWT) is kept in memory only; refresh token is in the encrypted MMKV "secure" instance. The axios instance in src/api/client.ts has a response interceptor that on 401 refreshes once (single-flight promise) and retries; a second 401 logs out.

After the FOR UPDATE fix, checkout occasionally failed with "psycopg.errors.DeadlockDetected: deadlock detected DETAIL: Process 812 waits for ShareLock on transaction 99812; blocked by process 815". Two carts locked the same variants in different orders. Fix: always lock inventory rows sorted by variant_id (ORDER BY variant_id in the FOR UPDATE query, and sort cart items before reserving). No deadlocks since 2026-06-02.

Incident 2026-07-22: ledger_unbalanced_total became 3 in production after a deploy, meaning three payments had unbalanced entries.

Root cause: a new partial-capture code path wrote the debit acquirer_clearing entry with the captured amount but the credit merchant_receivable with the authorized amount (variable shadowing: amount := req.AmountMinor inside an if block). The balance check trigger did not catch it because at the time it was a non-deferred row-level trigger that only checked after each statement on the inserting statement's rows — the two inserts were separate statements and the check was skipped for multi-currency payments by a bug in the WHERE clause.

Fixes: the check is now a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint trigger evaluated at commit for every touched payment_id; the service builds ledger entries with a helper ledger.Balanced(entries...) that returns an error if they do not sum to zero before hitting the DB; the shadowing pattern is caught by govet's shadow analyzer, now enabled in .golangci.yml. The three payments were corrected with adjustment entries per the ledger rules (no updates).

paygate is a Go 1.22 gRPC service that fronts card acquiring for internal clients. API: proto/paygate/v1/payments.proto (service PaymentService: Authorize, Capture, Void, Refund, GetPayment) managed with buf (buf.yaml, buf.gen.yaml generating Go with protoc-gen-go and protoc-gen-go-grpc into gen/). grpc-gateway v2 exposes the same RPCs as REST on :8081 for the admin UI; gRPC listens on :9090. Storage is Postgres 16 accessed with pgx v5 and sqlc (queries in internal/store/queries/*.sql, generated code in internal/store/db). The acquirer is reached through an adapter interface internal/acquirer.Acquirer with implementations sandboxacq (the acquirer's sandbox) and fake (in-memory for tests).

Each payment write is one Postgres transaction that updates payments, appends to ledger_entries (double entry) and writes an outbox row; a separate relay goroutine publishes outbox rows to Kafka topic paygate.payment-events.v1. Layout: cmd/paygate/main.go, internal/server (gRPC handlers), internal/service (business logic), internal/store, internal/acquirer, internal/outbox.

Change detection: a file is rehashed only if size or mtime (nanoseconds) differs from the manifest row. On filesystems with 2-second mtime resolution (FAT32/exFAT USB drives) this caused constant rehashing, so mtime comparison tolerates 2s when the volume is detected as FAT via statfs f_type on Linux and the volume format on macOS.

Clients authenticate with mTLS: certificates issued by the internal cert-manager ClusterIssuer paygate-clients-ca, client_id taken from the certificate's URI SAN spiffe://internal.test/client/<name>. Server cert rotation is handled by reloading certs via tls.Config.GetCertificate reading from the mounted secret on each handshake (cached 1 min).

`fsync verify` reported every large file as modified: we compared the stored blake3 to the ETag, but multipart ETags are md5-of-md5s with a -N suffix, not content hashes. Verify now compares the x-amz-meta-fsync-blake3 metadata (HeadObject) and only falls back to size+ETag equality with the manifest when the metadata is absent (objects uploaded by other tools).

User rule: never run terraform apply locally against prod. All prod changes go through a PR with `atlantis plan` output reviewed and `atlantis apply -p prod-eks` after approval. Local `terraform plan` is fine with the read-only role terraform-readonly via aws-vault exec infra-readonly.

Black Friday 2026 load test (run 2026-11-04 against staging, locust 2.24, 600 concurrent users, scenario mix 70% browse / 20% add-to-cart / 10% checkout) results:

Baseline before tuning: p95 product page 340ms, p95 add-to-cart 520ms, checkout confirm p95 2.9s with 1.8% errors (mostly QueuePool timeouts and ParcelHub timeouts). Postgres CPU peaked at 78% on db.r6g.xlarge; the hot query was the category listing with ORDER BY popularity, which did a sequential scan of product_variants.

Changes made: added ix_product_variants_product_id_active partial index (WHERE is_active), cached category listings for 2 min (sf:catalog:category:{id}:page:{n}:v2), raised web HPA max replicas from 6 to 12, moved ParcelHub quote calls behind the 4s timeout with fallback rates, and bumped the worker emails queue concurrency to 8.

After: p95 product page 120ms, add-to-cart 180ms, checkout confirm 780ms, error rate 0.05% at 600 users; at 1000 users the bottleneck became Stripe API latency (~400ms per PaymentIntent create), which we cannot fix. Decision: run 12 web replicas fixed from Nov 27 to Dec 1 instead of relying on HPA warm-up.

Capture flow (internal/service/capture.go), the most delicate path in paygate:
1. Load payment with status check: must be authorized; partial capture allowed once (amount <= authorized), the remainder is released automatically by the acquirer.
2. Transition authorized -> capturing with the optimistic UPDATE ... WHERE status='authorized'; commit. This commit is deliberate: if the process dies after the acquirer call, the reconciler sees capturing and asks the acquirer instead of capturing twice.
3. Call acquirer Capture with Idempotency-Reference = payment_id + ":capture"; acquirer timeout 8s.
4. On success, one transaction: status capturing -> captured, ledger entries (debit acquirer_clearing, credit merchant_receivable:<merchant>, debit fees:acquirer / credit acquirer_clearing for the fee if the acquirer returns it), outbox PaymentCaptured, idempotency response stored.
5. On a definitive decline, capturing -> failed with the acquirer code; on timeout/unknown, leave capturing and return codes.Unavailable with retry info; the reconciler resolves within 5 minutes.
Capturing a payment whose authorization expired returns ErrInvalidState mapped to FailedPrecondition with reason AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED; clients must re-authorize.

Credentials are not stored in ferrosync's config. We rely on aws-config's default provider chain (env vars, ~/.aws/credentials profile via aws_profile = "..." in our profile, SSO, IMDS). Decided against our own keychain integration in v0.6 because the AWS chain already covers SSO and users asked to reuse existing AWS profiles.

Workload AWS access uses IRSA via modules/iam-irsa (role trust on the cluster OIDC provider, condition on system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa>). We have not migrated to EKS Pod Identity yet; new workloads still use IRSA for consistency. The service account annotation eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn is set in the Helm values.

ferrosync design principles written down in docs/design.md after v0.5, which the user wants respected in every change:
1. Never lose data: a remote object is only deleted when the plan says so, the plan is shown first (or --yes is passed), and guards (delete ratio, root marker) cannot be disabled by config, only by explicit flags per run.
2. The manifest is a cache, not the source of truth: everything must be recoverable from the bucket (`fsync verify --rebuild-manifest`). So no information may exist only in the manifest — e.g. the Windows reserved-name mapping is also encoded in object metadata x-amz-meta-fsync-orig-name (percent-encoded), not just in the manifest.
3. Idempotent runs: running the same push twice in a row must result in zero actions the second time. Integration test tests/idempotent_push.rs enforces it for every backend we test (S3 via MinIO, R2 mocked with a recorded fixture).
4. One direction per command: push uploads, pull downloads; no hidden bidirectional behaviour.
5. Boring output: plan output and --json are stable interfaces; changes need a changelog entry under "Output changes".
6. No background daemons: fsync is a run-to-completion CLI. Scheduling is left to cron/launchd/systemd timers, with example units in contrib/.

`fsync verify` HEADs every manifest entry (concurrency 64) and reports missing, size-mismatch, hash-mismatch. --repair re-uploads mismatches and removes manifest rows for files deleted locally. A full verify of 400k objects takes ~6 min on a 100 Mbit link because HEAD is cheap.

User wants `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean before any commit and prefers explicit error enums over anyhow in library crates. No unwrap() or expect() in ferrosync-core outside tests; use ? with context. Formatting with rustfmt default settings, edition 2021.

Chose Redis over RabbitMQ as the Celery broker for shopfront because we already run Redis 7 for Flask-Limiter and the cart cache, and our peak volume (~40 tasks/s on Black Friday) does not need RabbitMQ's routing features. Trade-off accepted: no true priority queues, so we split work across separate queues instead.

EKS upgrade runbook (docs/runbooks/eks-upgrade.md): staging first, one minor version at a time. Steps: check deprecated APIs with `kubent` and `pluto detect-helm`, bump cluster_version in live/<env>/eks, apply control plane, update add-ons (vpc-cni, coredns, kube-proxy, ebs-csi) to versions listed by `aws eks describe-addon-versions`, then let Karpenter drift replace nodes (drift is enabled; AMI alias al2023@latest). Status as of 2026-11-20: staging on 1.30, prod still on 1.29, prod upgrade planned for 2026-12-03.

Dependencies are pinned with uv pip compile (requirements/base.in -> base.txt, dev.in -> dev.txt) instead of Poetry. Chose uv for speed in CI (dependency install went from 90s to 8s) and because we do not publish shopfront as a package. Update with `make deps-upgrade PKG=flask`.

Data quality layers in ledgerflow:
1. Ingestion checks in the operator: row count of the extract vs `SELECT count(*)` on the replica for the same window, failing the task if the difference exceeds 0.5%.
2. dbt source freshness (warn 6h / error 12h).
3. dbt generic tests on staging primary keys and on marts (unique, not_null, relationships, accepted_values on status columns).
4. Singular tests for business rules, e.g. tests/assert_order_totals_match_items.sql (orders.total_cents = sum(items) + shipping - discount, tolerance 0) and tests/assert_ledger_balanced.sql for the paygate ledger export.
5. Anomaly checks: daily row counts of fct_orders compared with the trailing 28-day median; more than 40% drop alerts but does not fail.
Test failures with severity error stop downstream models via Cosmos task dependencies; severity warn tests only alert. Store test failures is enabled (store_failures: true) for marts so analysts can query AUDIT.<test_name>.

Interrupted runs left orphaned multipart uploads that kept costing storage. Now on Ctrl-C the executor aborts in-flight uploads with AbortMultipartUpload (best effort, 5s budget), and `fsync gc --uploads --older-than 24h` lists ListMultipartUploads and aborts stale ones. We also recommend a bucket lifecycle rule AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload after 7 days in the README.

Search ranking tuned in 2026-07 after complaints that accessories ranked above shoes: ORDER BY ts_rank_cd(search_vector, query, 32) * (1 + ln(1 + popularity_30d) * 0.3) DESC, with popularity_30d a column on products refreshed nightly from order_items. Queries are built with websearch_to_tsquery('simple', :q) so quotes and minus work. We tried ts_rank (not _cd) first; cover density gave better results for multi-word queries like "trail running shoe". Out-of-stock products are not hidden but get multiplied by 0.5. The tuning was validated against 120 manually labelled queries in tests/search/relevance_cases.yaml; run `pytest tests/search -m relevance` after changing the formula and keep NDCG@10 above 0.78 (it was 0.81 at merge).

On Windows, files under deeply nested folders failed with "The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)" once paths exceeded 260 characters. Fix: canonicalize the sync root with dunce and prefix with \\?\ for I/O via std::path verbatim paths in crates/ferrosync-core/src/fs.rs. S3 keys always use forward slashes; backslashes are converted when building keys and rejected in .fsyncignore patterns with a helpful error.

Product detail page p95 regressed from 120ms to 650ms after the 2026-10-02 release. Profiling with py-spy on a staging pod (py-spy record -o profile.svg --pid <gunicorn worker> --duration 30) showed 70% of the time in Jinja rendering a macro called per variant, which itself called the money filter and babel.numbers.format_currency for each of ~40 variants x 3 prices, and babel locale loading was not cached because we passed locale as a string each time.

Fix: resolve the babel Locale object once per request (g.locale_obj) and pass it to format_currency; precompute display prices in the view instead of inside the macro; cache the rendered variant selector partial per product and locale for 10 minutes (sf:catalog:pdp-variants:{product_id}:{locale}:v1), invalidated with the product cache. p95 back to 110ms. Added a performance smoke test in loadtest/ that fails CI if the PDP p95 against the seeded large dataset exceeds 250ms.

Test data uses factory_boy SQLAlchemyModelFactory in tests/factories.py with sqlalchemy_session_persistence="flush". The db_session fixture in tests/conftest.py opens a connection, begins a transaction, binds the session with join_transaction_mode="create_savepoint" and rolls back after each test, so factories never commit real data.

Ingestion operator design (dags/ingest/operators/pg_to_snowflake.py, class PostgresToSnowflakeOperator):
1. Determine the window: for tables with updated_at, from the last high-water mark stored in Snowflake RAW._INGEST_STATE (source, table, hwm) minus a 15 minute overlap; for append-only tables by id range.
2. Extract with a server-side cursor (psycopg named cursor, itersize 50k) from the read replica, writing Parquet row groups of 100k rows with an explicit pyarrow schema per table (dags/ingest/schemas/*.py) to s3://example-ledgerflow-landing/<source>/<table>/<run_id>/part-*.parquet.
3. COPY INTO RAW.<SOURCE>.<TABLE> FROM @landing_stage/<path> FILE_FORMAT=(TYPE=PARQUET) MATCH_BY_COLUMN_NAME=CASE_INSENSITIVE, adding _loaded_at and _run_id via a transform.
4. Validate counts (extract vs replica count for the same window, tolerance 0.5%) and then advance the high-water mark in the same Snowflake transaction as a final step.
Replica lag is checked first (SELECT now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp()); if lag > 10 minutes the task retries up to 6 times with 10 minute delay instead of extracting stale data. The operator emits a Dataset event on success, which triggers dbt_daily.

CI runs `buf lint` and `buf breaking --against '.git#branch=main'` on proto changes. Field numbers are never reused; removed fields are listed in reserved. New RPCs go into v1 if additive; v2 package only for breaking changes. buf generate is pinned to buf 1.32 via the Makefile tool install.

Location permission flow (src/features/record/permissions.ts), designed with the store-review rejections in mind:
1. Before the first recording, show our own explainer screen, then request foreground "when in use" (iOS requestWhenInUseAuthorization / Android ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION).
2. Only when the user starts a recording and the screen locks for the first time do we ask for "always"/background on iOS (requestAlwaysAuthorization) — Apple rejected 2.1 for asking for always permission up front.
3. Android 10+ background location (ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION) is not requested at all: recording runs as a foreground service with a persistent notification, which Google Play accepted without the background location declaration form.
4. Android 13+: POST_NOTIFICATIONS is requested right before starting the foreground service, otherwise the service notification is hidden and users think recording stopped.
Denied states route to a settings deep link (Linking.openSettings()).

Postgres 14 -> 15 upgrade, status as of 2026-08-20: staging upgraded via pg_upgrade --link on 2026-08-12 with 6 min downtime; production is scheduled for the 2026-09-09 maintenance window. Checklist in docs/runbooks/pg15-upgrade.md: stop beat and workers first, run vacuumdb --analyze-in-stages afterwards, re-create the pg_trgm and citext extensions are not needed (they survive pg_upgrade), and update MIGRATIONS_DATABASE_URL host.

Black Friday 2025 postmortem (kept for reference): order confirmation emails were delayed up to 3 hours. All Celery tasks were on one default queue with one worker Deployment of concurrency 4; the hourly abandoned-cart batch enqueued ~180k email tasks at 10:00 and the confirmation tasks queued behind them. At the same time capture tasks were delayed, so a few hundred authorizations got close to expiring.

Changes that came out of it: separate queues default/emails/fulfillment with dedicated worker Deployments; abandoned-cart emails throttled with rate_limit="20/s" on the task and paused automatically via the pause_marketing_emails flag during peak days; confirmation emails get their own high-priority path by routing send_order_confirmation to emails while marketing sends go to a new emails_bulk queue consumed by a single low-concurrency worker. Monitoring: Grafana panel "celery queue length" per queue from the redis LLEN exporter, alert when emails > 5000 for 10 min.

Users were randomly logged out after resuming the app. Several queries fired at once on resume, all got 401, and each started its own refresh; the server rotates refresh tokens, so the second refresh used an already-rotated token and got 401 -> logout. Fix: single-flight refresh promise in src/api/client.ts shared by all concurrent 401s.

User convention: every model in marts has a schema.yml with unique + not_null on the primary key and relationships tests to dims; staging models test only primary keys. Use dbt_utils (1.2) and dbt_expectations sparingly; prefer singular tests in dbt/tests/ for business rules with a comment explaining the rule.

Build variants: three environments (development, staging, production) mapped to Android productFlavors dev/staging/prod (applicationId suffixes .dev and .staging) and iOS schemes trailmate-Dev, trailmate-Staging, trailmate with matching bundle identifiers and app icons with an environment badge. react-native-config reads .env.development / .env.staging / .env.production selected by ENVFILE in the scheme pre-actions and by the flavor in android/app/build.gradle (project.ext.envConfigFiles). API base URLs: https://api.dev.trailmate.test, https://api.staging.trailmate.test, https://api.trailmate.test. EAS profiles map to these: development -> dev flavor/scheme with developmentClient, preview -> staging (internal distribution), production -> prod (store). Mapbox public tokens differ per environment so usage stats stay separate.

Importing the supplier product feed (feeds/supplier_alpine.xml, ~900MB) with lxml.etree.parse got the import task OOMKilled. Fix: lxml.etree.iterparse(path, events=("end",), tag="item") and elem.clear() plus deleting previous siblings after each item; memory now flat at ~80MB. Import runs weekly via `flask catalog import-feed alpine`.

Benchmarks live in crates/ferrosync-core/benches (criterion 0.5): scan_10k_files, diff_100k_entries, plan_render. Run `cargo bench -p ferrosync-core -- --save-baseline main` before a change and `--baseline main` after. diff_100k_entries is ~38ms on M2; regression budget 10%.

Plan rendering (crates/ferrosync-cli/src/render.rs): the plan is a sorted Vec<Action>; human output groups by kind in fixed order Conflict, Delete, Upload, Skip, with counts and total bytes per group, then a summary line "upload 1,204 files (3.2 GiB), delete 0, conflicts 2". Deletes are printed in red and always listed in full even with --quiet, because hiding them caused the 0.4 incident to go unnoticed.

--json emits one JSON object per action ({"kind":"upload","path":"...","size":123,"reason":"modified"}) and a final {"kind":"summary",...}; field names are part of the stable interface documented in docs/json-output.md and covered by insta snapshots. Reasons are: new, modified (size or hash), metadata-only (mode changed with --preserve-mode), remote-missing (with --verify-remote), local-deleted. Adding a reason is fine, renaming one is a breaking change.

Returns (RMA) status as of 2026-11-10: customers can request a return from the order page within 30 days (returns table + return_items, status requested/approved/received/refunded). Approval is manual in admin. Not done yet: printable return labels from ParcelHub and automatic refund on received; refunds are still triggered manually via create_refund.

Mobile API auth flow (app/api/auth.py): POST /api/v1/auth/token with email + password (or a magic-link code) returns an opaque access token (32 bytes, urlsafe base64) once; only its sha256 is stored in api_tokens with device_name, created_at, last_used_at. Every request goes through the bearer token loader: hash the header value, look up api_tokens joined with customers, reject if customers.erased_at is set or the token is idle longer than 30 days.

Logout deletes the row; "log out everywhere" in account settings deletes all rows for the customer. Password reset also deletes all tokens. There is no refresh token: the token lives until idle expiry. Rate limits on the token endpoint are in Flask-Limiter (10/minute). Staff accounts cannot obtain API tokens at all (checked by role), because the admin uses session cookies with Flask-Login and the API has no admin endpoints.

Tests against MinIO failed with "dispatch failure: io error: error trying to connect: dns error: failed to lookup address information" for host fsync-test-abc.localhost. MinIO needs path-style addressing. Fix: when endpoint_url is set we build the client with force_path_style(true) in crates/ferrosync-s3/src/client.rs; virtual-hosted style stays the default for real S3.

User prefers running tests as `pytest -x -q --ff` and wants a failing test written before the fix for every bug. Keep test files mirroring app layout (tests/services/test_checkout.py for app/services/checkout.py). Do not use unittest.TestCase classes; plain functions with fixtures.

Integration tests run against MinIO started by tests/docker-compose.yml (minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-05-10T01-41-38Z on :9100, user fsynctest / fsynctest-secret). Run with `cargo test -p ferrosync-s3 --features integration -- --test-threads=4`. Each test creates a random bucket fsync-test-<uuid> and deletes it in a Drop guard.

Uploading a 40 GB VM image pushed RSS to ~9 GB. Each in-flight part buffered fully in memory (16 MiB x 4 parts x 16 files plus SDK retry buffers) and the auto-raised part size for huge files made parts ~500 MiB. Fix: parts stream from disk via ByteStream::read_from with offsets (no Vec buffering), and part concurrency for files over 10 GiB drops to 2. Peak RSS is now ~350 MB.

Investigation 2026-09-12: Metabase "Revenue by day" was 2-4% lower than finance's numbers for August.

Findings: (1) fct_orders excluded orders in status packed/shipped created before the 3h incremental lookback when their status changed days later — the merge only picked up rows by updated_at, but the replica's updated_at was not bumped by the state machine for status changes made via raw SQL in an ops script. (2) Refunds were subtracted by refund date while finance subtracts by order date. (3) Days were UTC instead of Berlin.

Fixes: the ingest now uses order_events max(created_at) as the change marker (greatest(updated_at, last_event_at)), a weekly full refresh of fct_orders runs Sunday 05:00, revenue models expose both refund_date and order_date based measures with documentation in models/marts/finance/_finance.yml, and order_date_berlin is the default date in the Metabase model. After fixes, August matched finance within 0.1% (remaining difference: currency rounding in two manual invoices).

Incident 2026-06-21: customers paying with 3D Secure cards came back from the bank page to /checkout/return and saw an empty cart and "Your session expired"; ~4% of card payments were affected for two days. The PaymentIntent had succeeded, so orders were stuck in pending_payment while customers often paid again (duplicate payments).

Root cause: we had changed the session cookie to SameSite=Strict in a security hardening PR. The bank's 3DS page returns via a top-level POST/redirect chain from another site, and the browser did not send a Strict cookie on that cross-site navigation, so Flask saw no session.

Fix: SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE back to "Lax" (Lax cookies are sent on top-level GET navigations, and Stripe's return_url redirect is a GET). Additionally /checkout/return no longer depends on the session at all: it looks up the order by payment_intent query param, verifies payment_intent_client_secret matches, and the payment_intent.succeeded webhook is the source of truth for moving the order to authorized. Duplicate payments were refunded via create_refund; 61 orders affected.

products.search_vector is a GENERATED ALWAYS AS (setweight(to_tsvector('simple', name), 'A') || ...) STORED column with a GIN index ix_products_search_vector. Alembic autogenerate does not detect changes to the generation expression; write the ALTER by hand with op.execute and drop/recreate the column. Use the 'simple' config because names are mixed German/English.

Stripe webhook events handled in app/webhooks/stripe.py: payment_intent.succeeded, payment_intent.payment_failed, payment_intent.canceled, charge.refund.updated, charge.dispute.created (creates an admin alert and freezes fulfillment). Everything else returns 200 and is ignored. Endpoint is /webhooks/stripe with API version pinned to 2024-06-20.

A user behind a corporate TLS-inspecting proxy got "invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer". rustls does not use the OS trust store by default. Fix: added rustls-native-certs so the system store is loaded, plus --ca-bundle for extra PEMs; native-tls feature remains as an alternative build.

`pod install` failed on Apple Silicon with "[!] CocoaPods could not find compatible versions for pod "MapboxMaps": In Podfile: rnmapbox-maps ... required MapboxMaps (= 10.16.4)" after bumping @rnmapbox/maps. Fix: set $RNMapboxMapsVersion = '= 10.16.4' at the top of ios/Podfile to match the package's expected version, then `cd ios && pod repo update && pod install`. Use Ruby 3.2 via rbenv, not system Ruby.

Incident 2026-06-09 during the staging EKS 1.28 -> 1.29 upgrade: after the control plane upgrade all new pods on Karpenter nodes failed with "networkPlugin cni failed to set up pod network: add cmd: Error received from AddNetwork gRPC call: rpc error: code = Unavailable" for ~40 minutes.

Root cause: we upgraded the vpc-cni add-on to v1.18 with configuration_values that dropped our custom networking settings (AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_CUSTOM_NETWORK_CFG and ENI_CONFIG_LABEL_DEF were set only by a manual kubectl set env earlier, not in Terraform). Nodes came up without ENIConfig and tried to allocate IPs from the exhausted primary subnets; the aws-node daemon then crashlooped on ipamd errors.

Fix: moved all vpc-cni env settings into the add-on configuration_values in live/<env>/eks/addons.tf (jsonencode({ env = { AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_CUSTOM_NETWORK_CFG = "true", ENI_CONFIG_LABEL_DEF = "topology.kubernetes.io/zone", ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION = "true", WARM_PREFIX_TARGET = "1" } })) with resolve_conflicts_on_update = "OVERWRITE", and the runbook now says to diff `kubectl -n kube-system get ds aws-node -o yaml` env before and after any add-on update.

Admin order list filtered by status=pending and sorted by created_at desc took 4s once orders passed 1.2M rows (seq scan). Added partial index ix_orders_pending_created ON orders (created_at DESC) WHERE status IN ('pending_payment','authorized'); query now 15ms. Remember EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on staging, not local, because local has 2k orders.

Amounts are int64 minor units plus ISO 4217 currency string (proto message Money { int64 amount_minor = 1; string currency = 2; }). No floats, no google.type.Money (its units+nanos split confused clients). Currencies with 0 or 3 decimal places (JPY, KWD) are handled via a table in internal/money/currency.go.

Windows support status as of 2026-11-05:
Works: push/pull/plan/status, long paths (verbatim \\?\ prefix), reserved-name mapping on pull, CRLF-agnostic .fsyncignore parsing, Ctrl-C handling via tokio::signal::ctrl_c.
Known issues: (1) file locking — files open in Outlook/Excel fail with "The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)"; we currently skip and report them as partial failures (exit 3), a VSS snapshot option is not planned; (2) mtime precision on network shares (SMB) is 100ns but some NAS devices round to 2s, causing rehash loops, same as the FAT issue — the tolerance setting [scan] mtime_tolerance_ms exists but auto-detection does not work on SMB; (3) the Windows CI runner does not run the MinIO integration tests, so S3 behaviour on Windows is only tested manually before releases.

dbt/macros/source_override.sql overrides source(): when target.name == 'dev' it returns RAW_SAMPLE.<schema>.<table> instead of RAW. Do not call adapter.get_relation in it (slow); it only rewrites the database name. Models must always use source()/ref(), never hardcoded RAW names, or this breaks.

After the aws-sdk-s3 1.66 upgrade, uploads to MinIO and older S3-compatible stores failed with "XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch" / "InvalidArgument: x-amz-checksum-crc32 header is not supported". The new SDK sends flexible checksums by default. Fix: .request_checksum_calculation(RequestChecksumCalculation::WhenRequired) on the S3 config when endpoint_url is set, and we compute CRC32C ourselves only for real AWS.

`fsync share <path> --expires 7d` prints a presigned GET URL built with PresigningConfig::expires_in (max 7 days for SigV4). It works only with credentials that are not short-lived beyond the expiry: with SSO session credentials the link dies when the session expires, which the command warns about.

Health endpoints: /healthz returns 200 if the process is up (no dependencies); /readyz checks Postgres (SELECT 1 with 1s timeout) and Redis PING. Kubernetes liveness uses /healthz and readiness /readyz; do not add Stripe or ParcelHub checks to readyz, a third-party outage must not pull all pods from the service.

To undo accidental deletes on a versioned bucket, `fsync restore --deleted-since 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z` lists ObjectVersions with IsLatest delete markers after the timestamp and deletes those markers (DeleteObject with VersionId), which makes the previous version current again. It never deletes real versions. Dry-run is the default; --apply executes.

Under load the web pods logged "sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30.00". Cause: each gthread worker held a connection across the ParcelHub HTTP call. Fix: release the session before external calls in checkout.py, and set pool_size=10, max_overflow=5, pool_pre_ping=True in app/db.py. Postgres max_connections is 200 and PgBouncer sits in front.

mypy runs in strict mode only for app/services and app/domain (see [tool.mypy] overrides in pyproject.toml); the rest of the code is checked with default settings. SQLAlchemy typing comes from the built-in 2.0 Mapped[] annotations, so the sqlalchemy-stubs plugin was removed.

After upgrading to Flask 3.0 the app crashed at import with "ImportError: cannot import name 'escape' from 'flask'" in app/templating.py. Use markupsafe.escape instead. Also before_first_request was removed; startup work moved into create_app.

Upgrading to Go 1.22 changed loop variable semantics; a test that captured the loop var in t.Parallel subtests started passing differently and revealed that two cases had always run with the last table entry. Not a production bug, but fixed the test data. Also bumped golangci-lint to 1.57 because older versions panicked with "go1.22 not supported".

Customer-facing order numbers look like SF-261126-K7Q2M: prefix SF, order date as YYMMDD, then 5 chars from an alphabet without 0/O/1/I. Generated in app/services/orders.py:generate_order_number and stored in orders.public_number (unique index). The integer orders.id is never shown to customers.

Every app Deployment with >= 2 replicas gets a PodDisruptionBudget (maxUnavailable 1) from the shared library chart k8s/charts/app-base. Karpenter consolidation respects PDBs; a PDB with minAvailable equal to replicas blocks node drain forever, which bit us once with Redis, so stateful sets use maxUnavailable 1 too.

User does not want blanket `# noqa` or `# type: ignore` comments; if a suppression is needed it must name the rule (e.g. `# noqa: S608` or `# type: ignore[arg-type]`) and have a short reason on the same line.

Android release build failed with "Execution failed for task ':app:mergeReleaseResources'. > Duplicate resources: ... values/values.xml [string/app_name]" after adding react-native-config. A flavor-specific strings.xml in android/app/src/staging/res duplicated app_name. Fix: resValue "string", "app_name", ... in productFlavors in build.gradle and delete the duplicate strings.xml.

macOS metadata files (.DS_Store, ._* AppleDouble files, Icon\r) and Windows Thumbs.db/desktop.ini are excluded by built-in default ignore patterns, which can be disabled with --no-default-ignores. Chose built-in defaults after most early bug reports were about .DS_Store churn.

pre-commit config (.pre-commit-config.yaml) runs ruff, ruff-format, check-yaml, end-of-file-fixer, the mjml-freshness local hook and a local hook that blocks commits containing "sk_live_" or "whsec_" followed by non-test values. Install with `pre-commit install` after cloning.

GET /api/v1/products/<id> raised "pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ProductOut variants Input should be a valid list [type=list_type, input_value=<sqlalchemy.orm.dynamic.AppenderQuery ...>]". Cause: Product.variants was a lazy="dynamic" relationship, which returns a query object, not a list. Fix: changed Product.variants to lazy="selectin" so it is a real list; dynamic relationships cannot be validated by pydantic.

Explore tab fetches trails with useInfiniteQuery on GET /v2/trails?bbox=...&cursor=..., staleTime 5 min, keyed by a bbox rounded to 3 decimals so small map pans reuse the cache. Map viewport changes are debounced 400 ms before refetching.

Throughput tuning results (2026-08, 1 Gbit link, eu-central-1, mix of 50k small files and 20 large files):
- --jobs 16 (default): 410 Mbit/s, small files dominate (per-request latency ~35ms).
- --jobs 64: 780 Mbit/s, CPU ~140% (TLS), no throttling errors.
- --jobs 128: 790 Mbit/s, occasional SlowDown under one prefix, not worth it.
- Part concurrency 4 vs 8 for large files: no difference above --jobs 32.
Recommendation documented in docs/performance.md: --jobs 64 for fast links, keep 16 for home connections because more parallel uploads hurt latency of other traffic. We did not raise the default because the bwlimit work is not finished and high defaults saturated users' uplinks (issue #74).

User wants small PRs (under ~400 changed lines), conventional commit messages (feat:, fix:, refactor:), and a migration in its own PR when it touches orders or inventory so it can be deployed and observed separately. Always mention the Alembic revision id in the PR description.

Events use the transactional outbox pattern (outbox table + relay) instead of publishing to Kafka directly after commit, because a crash between commit and publish lost two capture events in the prototype. The relay polls with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 100, publishes with franz-go (kgo) with idempotent producer enabled, then deletes rows. Ordering per payment is kept by using payment_id as the Kafka key.

After upgrading to Reanimated 3.10 the app crashed on launch with "[Reanimated] Failed to create a worklet. Did you forget to add Reanimated Babel plugin in babel.config.js?". The plugin was present but not last in the plugins array (module-resolver was after it). 'react-native-reanimated/plugin' must be the last plugin; then `yarn start --reset-cache`.

MSRV is Rust 1.74 (rust-version in workspace Cargo.toml), checked by a CI job using dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.74. aws-sdk-s3 releases regularly raise their MSRV, so aws-* crates are pinned with = versions in Cargo.toml and bumped together in one PR after checking the MSRV job.

Logging uses structlog with JSON output (app/logging.py). RequestIdMiddleware takes X-Request-ID from the ingress or generates a uuid4 and binds request_id, customer_id and route into contextvars; Celery tasks re-bind request_id from task headers so one checkout can be traced from web to worker in Loki with {app="shopfront"} | json | request_id="...".

ArgoCD showed kube-prometheus-stack permanently OutOfSync on the CRDs ("metadata.annotations: Too long: must have at most 262144 bytes" on apply). Large CRDs exceed the last-applied annotation limit with client-side apply. Fix: syncOptions ServerSideApply=true on that Application, plus Replace=true is not needed anymore.

--include / --exclude flags take globset patterns relative to the sync root and are evaluated after .fsyncignore; the last matching flag wins, mirroring rsync semantics. Patterns ending in / match directories only. Implemented in crates/ferrosync-core/src/filter.rs with GlobSetBuilder and literal_separator(true).

Deep links: scheme trailmate:// and universal links https://trailmate.test/t/<trailId> and /h/<hikeId>. Linking config in src/navigation/linking.ts maps t/:trailId -> TrailDetail, h/:hikeId -> HikeDetail. The apple-app-site-association file is served by the API project; Android assetlinks.json SHA-256 must include both the upload key and the Play app signing key.

Frontend assets: Tailwind CSS 3.4 and esbuild 0.20 via npm scripts (npm run build:css, build:js); outputs go to app/static/dist with content hashes and a manifest.json read by the asset_url() Jinja helper. HTMX and Alpine.js 3 are vendored in assets/vendor, no CDN.

Chose Zustand over Redux Toolkit for client state because the app has few global stores and recording state updates at 1 Hz; Zustand selectors avoid re-rendering the map screen. Server state stays in TanStack Query; do not copy API data into Zustand stores.

dbt_daily sometimes never started: it used an ExternalTaskSensor on ingest_shopfront with mode='poke', and on busy nights all 16 worker slots were taken by poking sensors waiting for each other. Replaced sensors with Dataset scheduling (ingest tasks have outlets=[Dataset("snowflake://raw/shopfront")]); dbt_daily schedule=[those datasets].

Stripe can deliver the same webhook event more than once. Every handler first inserts the event id into processed_events (event_id PRIMARY KEY, received_at) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; if no row was inserted the event is a duplicate and we return 200 immediately. The insert and the business change happen in one transaction.

Order state machine (app/domain/order_state.py): draft -> pending_payment -> authorized -> packed -> shipped -> delivered, with cancelled reachable from draft/pending_payment/authorized and returned reachable from delivered. Transitions are only made through OrderStateMachine.transition(order, event), which writes order_events rows; direct assignment to order.status is blocked by a SQLAlchemy validates hook.

check_inventory_ledger reported drift for 214 variants on 2026-10-30 (inventory.on_hand differed from the sum of inventory_movements by 1-3 units).

Cause: the admin "quick stock edit" form (app/admin/inventory.py) updated inventory.on_hand directly without writing an inventory_movements row, added by a contractor in September. Kestrel's nightly stock report then wrote adjustments relative to the edited values, so both numbers were "right" from their point of view but disagreed.

Fix: quick edit now calls app/services/inventory.py:adjust_stock(variant_id, delta, reason, actor), which writes the movement and updates on_hand in one transaction; a Postgres trigger now rejects UPDATEs of inventory.on_hand when the session variable shopfront.inventory_writer is not set (SET LOCAL by adjust_stock and commit/restock paths). Drift was corrected with one-off adjustment movements (reason='ledger-repair-2026-10-30').

Product search uses Postgres full-text search (tsvector column products.search_vector, weighted A for name, B for brand, C for description) instead of Elasticsearch. Catalog is ~18k variants, so a separate cluster was not worth the ops cost. Revisit if catalog passes ~500k rows or if we need typo tolerance beyond pg_trgm.

Snowflake auth started failing after the password policy change with "250001: Could not connect to Snowflake backend after 0 attempt(s). Aborting: JWT token is invalid". The public key fingerprint registered on SVC_AIRFLOW did not match the rotated private key. Fix: ALTER USER SVC_AIRFLOW SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2=... then switch, so rotation has no downtime; profiles.yml uses private_key_path from env.

Incident 2026-05-29 (oversell during the spring sale): 37 orders were accepted for variant SKU RUN-AIR-42-BLK while only 12 units were in stock. Root cause: reserve_stock in app/services/inventory.py read inventory.on_hand - inventory.reserved, checked availability in Python, then issued an UPDATE. Two checkout requests in different gthread workers interleaved between the read and the write, both saw enough stock, and both reserved.

Fix: the availability check and increment are now a single locked operation. reserve_stock does SELECT ... FROM inventory WHERE variant_id = ANY(:ids) ORDER BY variant_id FOR UPDATE, re-checks on_hand - reserved >= qty for each row inside the same transaction, then inserts inventory_reservations and updates inventory.reserved. We considered an UPDATE ... WHERE on_hand - reserved >= :qty RETURNING single statement; it is faster but made partial-failure reporting for multi-item carts awkward, so we kept row locks.

We also added a CHECK constraint inventory_reserved_le_on_hand (reserved <= on_hand) as a last line of defence; violating it raises IntegrityError, which checkout maps to OutOfStockError. Affected customers got a voucher; ops cancelled the 25 extra orders from the admin. Regression test: tests/integration/test_concurrent_reservation.py spins up 20 threads against one variant with 5 units and asserts exactly 5 succeed.

Stripe webhook endpoint returned 400 with "stripe.error.SignatureVerificationError: No signatures found matching the expected signature for payload". Cause: the view used request.get_json() and re-serialized it. stripe.Webhook.construct_event needs the raw bytes: use request.get_data() (as_text=False) and the STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (whsec_test_xxx locally from `stripe listen`).

User keeps architecture decision records in docs/adr/NNNN-title.md (MADR template) and wants a new ADR for any change to the ledger, the state machine or the outbox. Reference the ADR number in the PR title, e.g. "feat(ledger): fee accounts (ADR-0006)".

Secret rotation procedure for app credentials stored in Secrets Manager (e.g. prod/shopfront/stripe, prod/paygate/acquirer): 1) add the new value as a second key (e.g. STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_NEXT) or new version, 2) deploy apps that accept both if the provider supports overlap, 3) switch the primary key, 4) ESO picks it up within refreshInterval (1h) — force with `kubectl annotate externalsecret <name> force-sync=$(date +%s) --overwrite`, 5) Reloader restarts the Deployment, 6) revoke the old credential at the provider. Database passwords are rotated by RDS-managed secrets for paygate; shopfront still uses a static password rotated manually twice a year (ticket INFRA-240 to move it to RDS-managed).

As of 2026-10-03 the SQLAlchemy 2.0 style migration is half done: app/repositories/orders.py, products.py and customers.py use select() + Session.execute; carts.py, coupons.py and everything under app/admin still use the legacy Query API (session.query). SQLALCHEMY_WARN_20=1 is set in CI so new legacy usage shows warnings. Do not mix both styles in one repository module.

CI matrix (.github/workflows/ci.yml): ubuntu-latest (stable, beta, 1.74), macos-14 (stable), windows-2022 (stable). Integration tests with MinIO run only on ubuntu because Docker is not available on the macOS runners. Caching via Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 keyed on the Cargo.lock hash.

trailmate is a React Native 0.74 app (bare workflow, not Expo managed, but using expo-modules for a few packages) for planning and recording hikes. Hermes is enabled on both platforms. Navigation: React Navigation 6 with a root native-stack (AuthStack / MainTabs) and bottom tabs Explore, Record, Library, Profile. State: Zustand stores in src/stores (useRecordingStore, useAuthStore, useSettingsStore) with persistence through react-native-mmkv; server data via TanStack Query 5 against the trailmate API (https://api.trailmate.test/v2). Maps: @rnmapbox/maps 10.1 with offline packs. Recording: react-native-background-geolocation is NOT used (license cost); we wrote a native module LocationRecorder (ios/LocationRecorder.swift, android/.../LocationRecorderModule.kt) that writes points to SQLite via op-sqlite and emits batched events every 5s.

Folder layout: src/features/<feature>/{screens,components,hooks,api.ts}; shared UI in src/ui; native modules in src/native. Path aliases @/ -> src/ configured in babel.config.js (module-resolver) and tsconfig paths.

Crash reporting: @sentry/react-native 5 with source maps uploaded by the sentry-cli step in EAS build hooks (eas-build-post-install / on-success). Release name trailmate@<version>+<build>. Native crashes on Android need the debug symbols upload enabled with uploadNativeSymbols in sentry.gradle.

Admin dashboard widgets (app/admin/dashboard.py) show today's revenue, orders by status and low-stock variants (on_hand - reserved < 5). Values come from a materialized view admin_daily_stats refreshed every 5 minutes by a beat task, because computing revenue live on 1.2M orders was too slow.

cmd/reconcile runs as a Kubernetes CronJob every 5 minutes: finds payments in authorizing/capturing older than 5 min, asks the acquirer GetStatus, and finalizes them through the same service methods (writing ledger entries + outbox). It also does a daily settlement-file reconciliation at 06:00 UTC comparing the acquirer's settlement CSV against captured payments, writing mismatches to reconciliation_issues.

Source freshness: sources.yml declares loaded_at_field: _loaded_at with warn_after 6h and error_after 12h for shopfront and billing sources. dbt_daily runs `dbt source freshness` first via a Cosmos task; on error the run stops and Slack-like alerting (webhook to #data-alerts on the fake chat host) fires through on_failure_callback.

ExternalSecret stuck with status SecretSyncedError: "could not get secret data from provider: ResourceNotFoundException: Secrets Manager can't find the specified secret." The key had a typo, but also: ESO uses the secret name, not ARN, and our names are prefixed by env (prod/shopfront/stripe). Use remoteRef.key: prod/shopfront/stripe with property STRIPE_SECRET_KEY.

Mapbox needs two tokens: the public access token pk.test_xxx set at runtime via Mapbox.setAccessToken from react-native-config (.env MAPBOX_PUBLIC_TOKEN), and a secret downloads token sk.test_xxx in ~/.netrc (machine api.mapbox.com) for iOS pod downloads and in gradle.properties MAPBOX_DOWNLOADS_TOKEN for Android. CI reads both from GitHub secrets.

Celery tasks in the fulfillment queue were executing twice: export_orders_to_kestrel takes ~70 minutes on big days and the Redis broker redelivered it after the default visibility_timeout of 3600s. Fix: broker_transport_options={"visibility_timeout": 14400} in app/celery_config.py, plus the task now takes a Redis lock (fulfillment:export:lock) so a redelivery exits early.

Capture in the packed webhook failed for some orders with "stripe.error.InvalidRequestError: This PaymentIntent could not be captured because it has a status of canceled". Those authorizations had expired after 7 days because Kestrel packing was delayed. Now flag_expiring_authorizations alerts at day 6 and the capture task, on this error, creates a new PaymentIntent off_session with the saved payment method or moves the order to cancelled and emails the customer.

Navigation conventions in trailmate (src/navigation/): typed routes via RootStackParamList and per-tab ParamLists declared in src/navigation/types.ts, with the global ReactNavigation.RootParamList augmentation so useNavigation() is typed without generics. Screens receive only ids in params (trailId, hikeId), never whole objects, so deep links and state restoration work and TanStack Query provides the data.

The recording screen is presented as a fullScreenModal on the root stack, not inside the Record tab, so that switching tabs during a recording is impossible and the modal survives tab resets. Android hardware back on the recording modal shows a "stop recording?" sheet (usePreventRemove from React Navigation 6.1). Navigation state persistence is enabled only in dev builds (__DEV__) to speed up reloads; in production the app always starts on Explore unless a recording is active, in which case the root navigator's initialRouteName is RecordingModal based on useRecordingStore.getState().activeHikeId read synchronously from MMKV before the first render.

Incremental models (fct_orders, fct_order_items, fct_payments) use materialized='incremental', incremental_strategy='merge', unique_key the natural id, and filter with where updated_at > (select dateadd(hour, -3, max(updated_at)) from {{ this }}) — the 3-hour lookback catches late-arriving updates from the replica lag. Full refresh only via the manual DAG dbt_full_refresh with a model selector param.

Atlantis plan failed with "Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException ... Lock Info: ID: 5f1c... Path: example-tfstate-eu-central-1/prod/eks/terraform.tfstate Operation: OperationTypeApply Who: atlantis@atlantis-0". A previous apply pod was killed mid-run. After confirming no apply is running (atlantis UI + kubectl get pods -n atlantis), run `atlantis unlock` on the PR or `terraform force-unlock 5f1c...` from the root with the same backend config.

Alembic conventions in shopfront (migrations/README.md summarises them):
- File names are generated with a date prefix: file_template = %%(year)d%%(month).2d%%(day).2d_%%(rev)s_%%(slug)s in alembic.ini.
- Every migration sets op.execute("SET lock_timeout = '5s'") (done centrally in env.py) and statement_timeout 15min.
- Indexes on large tables (orders, order_items, inventory_movements, order_events) are created with postgresql_concurrently=True inside op.get_context().autocommit_block(), because CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY blocks writes on orders for minutes.
- No data backfills inside migrations for tables over 100k rows; use a one-off Celery task or flask command in batches of 5000 with a sleep.
- downgrade() must be implemented unless the migration is explicitly irreversible, in which case it raises RuntimeError with a reason.
- Autogenerate output is always reviewed: it misses changes to generated columns, CHECK constraints and server defaults on enums.
- Enum types: we use VARCHAR + CHECK constraints, not Postgres ENUM, because adding values to a Postgres ENUM cannot run inside a transaction on older versions and caused trouble once.

User wants all distance logic in meters and conversions only in src/utils/units.ts formatDistance/formatElevation (km/mi, m/ft based on useSettingsStore.units). No inline toFixed or unit math in components; reviewers reject it.

Inventory lifecycle: reserve (checkout start: inventory.reserved += qty, reservation row with 15 min expiry) -> commit (payment authorized: reservation row deleted, inventory.reserved -= qty, inventory.on_hand -= qty, inventory_movements row type=sale) -> release (expiry or cancel: reserved -= qty). Restocks from Kestrel stock reports insert inventory_movements type=restock. inventory.on_hand must always equal the sum of inventory_movements for that variant; a nightly check_inventory_ledger task reports drift.

VAT is computed per order line and rounded half-up to the cent per line, then summed, rather than rounding once on the order total. Chosen because invoices from the accounting system show per-line VAT and totals must match to the cent. Implemented in app/services/tax.py with Decimal and ROUND_HALF_UP; results are converted back to integer cents.

PgBouncer 1.21 runs as a sidecar-less Deployment in front of Postgres in transaction pooling mode (default_pool_size 40). Consequences we hit: session-level advisory locks (pg_advisory_lock) do not work, so the fulfillment export uses a Redis lock instead; server-side prepared statements must be disabled with psycopg prepare_threshold=None in the engine connect_args. Alembic migrations bypass PgBouncer and connect to postgres-primary directly via MIGRATIONS_DATABASE_URL, because ALTER TABLE ... with lock_timeout needs a stable session.

Incident 2026-07-14: after a psycopg upgrade, checkout errored with "psycopg.errors.DuplicatePreparedStatement: prepared statement "_pg3_0" already exists" for about 25 minutes because the prepare_threshold setting had been dropped in a refactor of app/db.py. Fix restored the connect_args and added tests/test_db_config.py asserting the engine options. Rule: never remove prepare_threshold=None while PgBouncer is in transaction mode.

Load test 2026-10-14 with ghz (`ghz --proto proto/paygate/v1/payments.proto --call paygate.v1.PaymentService.Authorize -c 200 -n 100000 --cert ...`) against staging with the sandbox acquirer stubbed at 150ms: 1,850 RPS at p99 310ms with 6 pods; the bottleneck was the ledger balance trigger. Moving check_ledger_balanced to a deferred constraint trigger per statement brought p99 to 240ms.

Elevation profile chart uses victory-native XL (Skia-based) instead of react-native-svg-charts, which is unmaintained and dropped frames on 5k-point profiles. The profile is downsampled to 300 points with LTTB (largest triangle three buckets) in src/features/trail/elevation.ts before rendering.

User asked that every bug involving paths gets a regression test with non-ASCII names (umlauts, CJK, emoji) and a Windows-reserved name check (CON, aux.txt). Put these in crates/ferrosync-core/tests/paths.rs.

When a guest with a cart logs in, the guest cart is merged into the customer's saved cart in app/services/carts.py:merge_on_login: quantities for the same variant are summed and capped at the per-variant max of 10, then the guest cart row is deleted. Chose merge over "guest cart wins" after support tickets about items disappearing.

Backfills: never use the Airflow CLI `airflow dags backfill` for dbt (it creates hundreds of Cosmos task instances). For ingestion, trigger ingest_<source> with conf {"start": "2026-01-01", "end": "2026-02-01"}; the operator chunks by day. For dbt, run dbt_full_refresh with a selector, or a one-off `dbt run -s fct_orders --vars '{"backfill_start": "2026-01-01"}'` which the incremental filter respects.

Atlantis plan for live/prod/network wanted to remove tags on 40 subnets: "~ tags = { - "karpenter.sh/discovery" = "prod-eu1" }". The tags had been added by hand during the Karpenter rollout. Fix: add them in modules/vpc via var.private_subnet_tags; rule: no console changes, and a nightly drift-detection workflow runs terraform plan -detailed-exitcode on all roots and opens an issue on exit code 2.

CI MSRV job failed after cargo update with "error: package `aws-smithy-runtime v1.5.6` cannot be built because it requires rustc 1.76 or newer, while the currently active rustc version is 1.74.1". Fix: revert Cargo.lock for aws-smithy-* with `cargo update -p aws-smithy-runtime --precise 1.5.5`. Decision pending whether to bump MSRV to 1.76.

Push notifications: Firebase Cloud Messaging for Android and APNs via FCM for iOS using @react-native-firebase/messaging 20. The device token is registered via POST /v2/devices after login and on token refresh (messaging().onTokenRefresh). Notification types: friend_finished_hike, weather_alert, offline_pack_ready. Tapping a notification navigates through the linking config using data.url (trailmate://hike/<id>). Notifee is used to show foreground notifications because FCM does not display them while the app is open. iOS requires the "Push Notifications" capability and the APNs auth key uploaded to Firebase; the GoogleService-Info.plist for staging and prod is selected by the scheme's pre-build script.

Intermittent 502s on shopfront during deploys with nginx logging "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream". Pods were removed from endpoints after SIGTERM, but nginx still had them in its upstream list for a few seconds. Fix: preStop hook sleep 10 in the app Deployments and terminationGracePeriodSeconds 40; also set the NLB deregistration delay to 30s.
