external-dns failed with "AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity". The role trust policy condition used the service account name external-dns but the chart created external-dns-sa. Fix the condition in live/prod/eks/irsa.tf (sub = system:serviceaccount:external-dns:external-dns-sa) and restart the pod so it gets a fresh token.

Inventory reservations are created when checkout starts (not at add-to-cart) and expire after 15 minutes. Celery beat runs release_expired_reservations every 60s on the default queue; it deletes inventory_reservations rows with expires_at < now() and decrements inventory.reserved. Chose checkout-time reservation because add-to-cart reservation locked stock for hours in abandoned carts.

Coupons do not stack: at most one coupon per order, enforced in app/services/coupons.py:apply_coupon and by a unique constraint on order_coupons(order_id). Product asked for stacking in August; we declined because percentage + fixed stacking made the tax rounding per line ambiguous. Free-shipping coupons are the one exception and are stored as a flag on carts, not in order_coupons.

Structlog contextvars leaked between requests: a log line for one customer carried another customer_id. With gthread workers, threads are reused and we bound context in before_request without clearing. Fix: structlog.contextvars.clear_contextvars() at the start of before_request and in teardown_request.

Incident 2026-09-23: the Redis primary was rescheduled to a new node and for 4 minutes everything depending on Redis failed: login returned 500 because Flask-Limiter raised "redis.exceptions.ConnectionError: Error -3 connecting to redis-master:6379. Temporary failure in name resolution", carts stored in Redis cache could not be read, and Celery workers stopped consuming.

What we changed: RATELIMIT_IN_MEMORY_FALLBACK_ENABLED=True and RATELIMIT_SWALLOW_ERRORS=True so rate limiting degrades instead of failing requests; cart reads fall back to Postgres (the cache is read-through, carts are persisted in the carts table anyway); Celery broker_connection_retry_on_startup=True and broker_connection_max_retries=None so workers reconnect forever. Redis now runs with a PodDisruptionBudget minAvailable 1 and a replica with Sentinel via the infra team's chart; the app connects through the Sentinel service name redis-sentinel:26379 with master name shopfront.

Postmortem action still open as of 2026-11-01: alert when the Celery queues have zero consumers for more than 2 minutes.

Deploy: the Helm chart deploy/helm/shopfront renders Deployments shopfront-web, shopfront-worker-default, shopfront-worker-emails, shopfront-worker-fulfillment, shopfront-beat, plus a pre-upgrade hook Job shopfront-migrate that runs `flask db upgrade` using the same image tag. GitHub Actions builds ghcr.io/example/shopfront:<sha> and the infra repo's ArgoCD Application tracks values-production.yaml image.tag. If the migrate Job fails, the hook blocks the rollout and old pods keep serving.

Manifest schema v3 migration (shipped in 0.9.0, 2026-10): added entries.remote_version_id and entries.etag columns, and moved the blake3 hash from hex TEXT to a 32-byte BLOB to shrink manifest.db by ~40% (412k entries: 118 MB -> 71 MB).

The migration runs automatically on first open via rusqlite_migration with a backup copy written to .ferrosync/manifest.db.bak-v2 first. It converts in batches of 10k rows in one transaction each so an interrupted migration can resume (meta.migration_progress tracks the last rowid). Downgrading fsync to 0.8.x after migrating fails with "manifest schema version 3 is newer than supported (2)"; the fix is to restore the .bak-v2 file. We decided not to support downgrade migrations because the manifest can always be rebuilt with `fsync verify --rebuild-manifest` (one HEAD per object).

GET /api/v1/orders took 2.8s for customers with 200 orders: one query per order for order_items and another per item for product_variants. Fixed in app/repositories/orders.py:list_for_customer with options(selectinload(Order.items).joinedload(OrderItem.variant)). Now 3 queries total, ~90ms. Added a pytest fixture assert_max_queries(n) in tests/conftest.py to guard it.

The outbox relay waits for work with LISTEN outbox_new on a dedicated pgx connection (pgxpool.Acquire, then conn.Conn().WaitForNotification(ctx)), with a 2s polling fallback; the insert trigger does pg_notify('outbox_new', ''). This is why paygate connects directly to Postgres without PgBouncer transaction pooling.

Celery task send_order_confirmation crashed with "sqlalchemy.orm.exc.DetachedInstanceError: Instance <Order at 0x7f...> is not bound to a Session; attribute refresh operation cannot proceed". The view passed the ORM object through .delay(). Rule now: tasks take primitive ids only (order_id: int) and open their own session via app.db.session_scope().

Clients saw "rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded" on Authorize while the acquirer call actually succeeded, leading to retries. Cause: the client deadline (3s) was shorter than the acquirer's p99 (2.6s) plus DB time. Fixes: the service checks ctx.Deadline() and rejects with codes.InvalidArgument if less than 5s remain; clients must set at least 10s for Authorize; retries are safe thanks to idempotency keys.

Ledger: ledger_entries(id, payment_id, account, direction debit|credit, amount_minor, currency, created_at) with accounts like merchant_receivable:<merchant>, acquirer_clearing, fees:acquirer, refunds_payable. Each business operation writes balanced entries in one transaction; a deferred constraint trigger check_ledger_balanced verifies sum(debits) = sum(credits) per payment_id and currency at commit. Capture writes debit acquirer_clearing / credit merchant_receivable; refunds reverse with refunds_payable. Never update or delete ledger rows; corrections are new entries with reason='adjustment'.

insta snapshot tests for `fsync plan` failed only on CI with differing order of actions. The plan was built from a HashMap iteration. Plans are now sorted by (action kind priority, path) before rendering, and the diff uses BTreeMap<RelPath, Entry> throughout ferrosync-core::diff.

All money in shopfront is stored as BIGINT cents (orders.total_cents, order_items.unit_price_cents, etc.), never NUMERIC or float. Chosen to match Stripe's integer amounts and avoid Decimal/float mixing in JSON. Formatting to "12,90 €" happens only in templates via the money filter in app/templating.py.

cert-manager 1.14 with ClusterIssuers letsencrypt-prod and letsencrypt-staging using DNS-01 via Route53 (IRSA role cert-manager-route53), because some hosts are behind an internal NLB where HTTP-01 is impossible. Ingresses request certs via annotation cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer. Internal CAs (paygate-clients-ca, paygate-clients-ca-staging) are CA issuers backed by secrets.

Tax calculation design (app/services/tax.py), written after the 2026-02 audit:

Rates come from the tax_rates table (country, tax_class, rate_bp in basis points, valid_from, valid_to), not from a third-party service. Tax classes are standard, reduced (books, some food) and zero. product_variants.tax_class defaults to standard. For B2C sales to other EU countries we apply destination-country VAT (OSS scheme) once the yearly threshold is passed; the flag oss_active in settings is true since 2025.

Prices in the catalog are gross (VAT included) as required for B2C display in Germany. For each order line we derive net = round_half_up(gross * 10000 / (10000 + rate_bp)) and tax = gross - net, per line, so the gross the customer saw never changes. Shipping is taxed at the rate of the dominant tax class in the cart by value (rule from our tax advisor). Reverse-charge B2B orders store gross = net.

Changing a rate: insert a new tax_rates row with valid_from; never update an existing row, because order_items store tax_rate_bp at purchase time and reports join on it. Tests in tests/services/test_tax.py contain the advisor's 14 worked examples; do not change their expected values.

No dbt Python models: Snowpark Python models were tried for a customer segmentation model but cold start of the Python warehouse added 2-3 minutes and debugging was hard. The segmentation runs as an Airflow PythonOperator writing to MARTS.CUSTOMER_SEGMENTS, declared as a dbt source with freshness.

MRR definition agreed with finance (2026-10): MRR on a day = sum of active subscriptions' monthly price excluding VAT, annual plans divided by 12, discounts applied, trials excluded, paused subscriptions excluded. Upgrades count at the new price from the effective date, not the invoice date. Documented in models/marts/finance/fct_mrr.md.

Redis cache keys in shopfront follow sf:{domain}:{entity}:{id}:v{schema_version}, e.g. sf:catalog:product:812:v3. Bump the version suffix in app/cache.py CACHE_VERSIONS when the cached shape changes instead of flushing Redis. TTLs: product 10 min, category listing 2 min, cart 24 h.

API responses use the envelope {"data": ..., "error": null, "meta": {...}} built by app/api/responses.py ok()/fail(). Errors carry {"code": "OUT_OF_STOCK", "message": "...", "details": {...}}. Pagination meta is cursor-based: {"next_cursor": "...", "limit": 50}; offset pagination is not used anywhere in /api/v1.

GDPR account deletion anonymizes rather than deletes. app/services/privacy.py:erase_customer replaces name, email (erased+<id>@invalid.test), phone and addresses, deletes carts, api_tokens and saved payment methods (Stripe customer deleted via API), but keeps orders and order_items because German tax law requires 10 years retention of invoices. erased_at is set on customers and the customer can no longer log in.

Requests come in via the account page or support; the admin action calls the same function. A nightly job checks that no erased customer has non-anonymized fields. We decided against hard delete with ON DELETE CASCADE in March after realizing it would remove order history needed for accounting exports and refunds.

Metabase reads only from MARTS through the METABASE role with a BI_WH warehouse. Models exposed to business users are tagged meta: {metabase: true} in schema.yml and documented; a nightly script syncs dbt descriptions into Metabase column descriptions via the Metabase API.

Outgoing mail goes through the fake relay mailrelay.example.test:587 with STARTTLS. Bounces and complaints arrive at POST /webhooks/mail and set customers.email_status = bounced|complained; send_* tasks skip customers whose email_status is not ok, except password resets.

The slowest tests are in tests/integration (marked @pytest.mark.integration) and are skipped locally by default via addopts = -m "not integration" in pyproject.toml. Run them with `pytest -m integration` (needs docker compose up for stripe-mock). CI runs both sets.

`fsync status` reads only the manifest and the local tree (no network) and prints counts of new, modified, deleted-locally and synced files plus the last run from the runs table. With --porcelain it prints one line per changed file: "M path", "A path", "D path".

Kestrel sends a full stock report as a JSON payload (stock_report event on /webhooks/kestrel) every night at 05:00 with on-hand counts per sku. apply_stock_report compares to inventory.on_hand and writes inventory_movements type=adjustment for differences larger than 0; differences above 20 units for one sku are only logged and need admin approval.

CI test job failed randomly with "redis.exceptions.ConnectionError: Error 111 connecting to localhost:6379. Connection refused." in the first tests. The redis service container was not healthy yet when pytest started. Fix: add options: --health-cmd "redis-cli ping" --health-interval 2s --health-retries 15 to the redis service in ci.yml, same as postgres already had.

New client got "transport: authentication handshake failed: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" against staging. Their cert came from the prod CA; staging trusts only paygate-clients-ca-staging. Client certs are per environment; issue from the matching ClusterIssuer.

manifest.db schema (crates/ferrosync-manifest/migrations/): table entries(path TEXT PRIMARY KEY, size INTEGER, mtime_ns INTEGER, blake3 BLOB, etag TEXT, remote_version_id TEXT, synced_at INTEGER), table runs(id, started_at, finished_at, status, uploaded, deleted, bytes), table meta(key, value) holding schema_version and the bucket/prefix the root is bound to. Migrations are embedded with rusqlite_migration. WAL mode and synchronous=NORMAL.

Config file: ~/.config/ferrosync/config.toml (XDG; on macOS also ~/Library/Application Support/ferrosync/config.toml is read if the XDG one is missing). Profiles: [profile.default] bucket, prefix, region, endpoint_url (for MinIO/R2), storage_class, sse. CLI flags override profile values; FSYNC_PROFILE selects a profile. Parsed with serde + toml 0.8 into ferrosync_core::config::Config.

NetworkPolicies are enforced with the VPC CNI network policy agent (enableNetworkPolicy: "true" on the vpc-cni add-on). Default-deny ingress in app namespaces (paygate, shopfront), with explicit allows from ingress-nginx and monitoring. paygate only accepts traffic from namespaces labelled paygate-client=true.

Offline maps: users download a region from the trail detail screen. src/features/offline/downloadRegion.ts calls offlineManager.createPack with styleURL outdoors-v12, bounds = trail bbox buffered by 2 km, minZoom 10, maxZoom 15. Packs are named trail:<trailId>:v1. A pack for a 20 km trail is ~35-60 MB. The Library tab lists packs from offlineManager.getPacks() and shows size from pack.status().completedResourceSize. Limit: Mapbox's default tile count limit of 6000 per account device was raised with offlineManager.setTileCountLimit(25000) at startup; above that, downloads fail with "Mapbox tile count limit exceeded".

Bug in 2.5.1 (reported 2026-10-12): users who downloaded offline packs for several trails could not open any map offline; the map showed grey tiles. Packs were present (Library showed them as complete).

Root cause: the style URL used for packs was mapbox://styles/mapbox/outdoors-v12 but the map component loaded our custom style mapbox://styles/trailmate-test/outdoors-tm-v3 since 2.5.0. Offline packs are tied to the style URL and its sources; the custom style referenced an extra vector source (our trail overlay) and a different sprite set, so tiles were not found in the offline cache.

Fix in 2.5.2: downloadRegion uses the same style URL constant (MAP_STYLE_URL in src/features/map/constants.ts) as the MapView, and on startup a migration deletes packs whose metadata.styleURL differs and offers the user to re-download them. Detox test added that downloads a small pack, toggles airplane mode via device.setURLBlacklist(['.*']) and asserts the tile-loaded event fires.

SQLAlchemy 2.0 migration plan, decided 2026-09-01 after the Flask 3 upgrade:

Why: the legacy Query API emits RemovedIn20Warning, typing with Mapped[] only works properly with select(), and session.query in admin code was the source of three N+1 bugs this year because it hid lazy loads.

How: module by module inside app/repositories, never a big bang. Each module PR (1) converts queries to select()/session.scalars()/session.execute(), (2) sets lazy="raise_on_sql" on the relationships it touches so missing eager loads fail tests instead of silently querying, (3) adds an assert_max_queries test for each list endpoint using it. Order: orders, products, customers (done), then carts, coupons, admin (remaining). The admin conversion also removes the last uses of Model.query (the Flask-SQLAlchemy property) so we can drop Flask-SQLAlchemy in favour of a plain sessionmaker in app/db.py.

Known gotcha: session.execute(select(Order)) returns Row objects; use session.scalars() when you want ORM instances, otherwise templates fail with "AttributeError: 'Row' object has no attribute 'public_number'".

shipments table: id, order_id, carrier (dhl|ups|dpd), tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at, kestrel_parcel_id. Orders can have multiple shipments for split parcels. sync_tracking_status task polls ParcelHub /tracking every 2h for shipments without delivered_at younger than 21 days and transitions orders to delivered.

ferrosync architecture (crate layout as of v0.9): a Cargo workspace with crates/ferrosync-cli (clap 4 binary `fsync`), crates/ferrosync-core (scan, diff, plan, execute), crates/ferrosync-s3 (wrapper over aws-sdk-s3 1.x), and crates/ferrosync-manifest (local state in SQLite via rusqlite 0.31, file .ferrosync/manifest.db in the sync root).

A sync run is: scan (walk the local tree with the ignore crate, honouring .fsyncignore and .gitignore) -> hash (blake3, only for files whose size or mtime changed since the manifest) -> diff (compare local entries, manifest entries and, with --verify-remote, a ListObjectsV2 listing) -> plan (a Vec<Action> of Upload, Delete, Skip, Conflict) -> execute (tokio runtime, bounded concurrency with a Semaphore, default 16 transfers). The manifest is updated after each successful action, not at the end, so an interrupted run resumes without re-uploading.

Errors use thiserror in library crates (CoreError, S3Error, ManifestError) and anyhow only in the CLI crate. Logging is tracing with tracing-subscriber; -v sets info, -vv debug, RUST_LOG overrides.

Acquirer HTTP client: 8s total timeout, no automatic retries for Authorize and Capture (not idempotent at the acquirer unless we send their Idempotency-Reference header, which we now do), retries with backoff for GetStatus. Circuit breaker sony/gobreaker opens after 50% failures over 20 requests, half-open after 30s; when open Authorize returns codes.Unavailable.

charge.dispute.created handling: sets orders.disputed=true, creates an admin_alerts row (severity high), and if the order is not shipped yet, blocks fulfillment by excluding disputed orders from the Kestrel export. Evidence submission is manual in the Stripe dashboard; there is no automation for it.

Addresses: customer_addresses (customer_id, label, name, line1, line2, postal_code, city, country_code ISO-3166 alpha-2, phone, is_default_shipping, is_default_billing). Orders do not reference customer_addresses; they copy shipping_* and billing_* columns at checkout so later edits do not change past orders.

Validation happens in app/services/addresses.py: postal codes are checked with per-country regexes for DE, AT, CH, FR, NL, BE (others only length-checked), and country_code must be in SHIPPING_COUNTRIES. ParcelHub has an address validation endpoint, but we only call it for packstation addresses (line1 starting with "Packstation"), where we also require the 6-10 digit postnummer in line2. Kestrel rejects addresses with lines longer than 35 characters, so the form enforces maxlength=35 on line1/line2 and the export truncates defensively with a warning in the logs.

Databases: RDS Postgres 15 for shopfront (db.r6g.xlarge, Multi-AZ, 500GB gp3, Performance Insights on) and Postgres 16 for paygate (db.r6g.large, Multi-AZ), defined in live/prod/data with modules/rds. Parameter groups set log_min_duration_statement=500, rds.force_ssl=1. Backups: RDS automated backups (14 days, PITR) plus the AWS Backup plan prod-daily with 35-day retention and a monthly copy to the backup account.

Server-side encryption: profile sse = "aws:kms" with sse_kms_key_id = "arn:aws:kms:eu-central-1:000000000000:key/test-key-id" sets ServerSideEncryption and SSEKMSKeyId on PutObject and CreateMultipartUpload. With KMS, ETags are not MD5s, another reason verify uses blake3 metadata. Default is sse = "AES256".

Mobile app showed duplicated orders when scrolling the order history. Cursor was created_at only and several orders shared the same created_at (bulk import). Fix: cursor encodes (created_at, id) as base64 JSON and the query uses WHERE (created_at, id) < (:c, :i) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC with index ix_orders_customer_created_id.

CI (.github/workflows/dbt.yml): on PR, `dbt deps`, `dbt build --select state:modified+ --defer --state prod-artifacts/` against a per-PR schema CI_PR_<number> in the DEV database, with prod manifest downloaded from the artifacts bucket. A nightly job drops CI_PR_* schemas older than 7 days. sqlfluff lint runs only on changed files.

Bug report #131 (2026-08-03): after a laptop sleep during `fsync push`, some files were marked synced in the manifest although the upload had not completed; the next push skipped them, so the bucket had stale versions.

Root cause: the manifest row was written when the CompleteMultipartUpload future was created, not after it resolved, due to an early `manifest.mark_synced(&entry)` before `.await?` in execute.rs after a refactor in 0.8.1. On wake, the TCP connection was dead, the SDK returned a timeout error, but the manifest commit had already happened.

Fix in 0.8.2: mark_synced is called only after a successful response and receives the returned ETag and VersionId, which are stored; a debug assertion checks that etag is Some. Added a fault-injection test using a MinIO proxy (toxiproxy) that drops the connection during CompleteMultipartUpload and asserts the manifest is unchanged. Users affected were told to run `fsync verify --repair`, which re-uploads entries whose remote ETag does not match the manifest.

Files with umlauts uploaded from macOS appeared twice in the bucket after syncing the same folder from Linux: "Müller.txt" was NFD on APFS (from older HFS+ copies) and NFC on Linux, so the keys differed. Now keys are normalized to NFC with unicode-normalization before diffing and uploading; a one-off `fsync doctor --fix-nfd` renames old NFD keys with CopyObject + DeleteObject.

TypeScript strict with noUncheckedIndexedAccess; user prefers type-only imports (import type) and no default exports except screens (React Navigation screen components are default exports for lazy loading). Lint with eslint @react-native config plus @typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports.

Admin is a custom blueprint (app/admin) built with Jinja + HTMX 1.9, not Flask-Admin. Flask-Admin was tried in February but its model views bypassed our service layer (orders could change status without OrderStateMachine) and theming fought with Tailwind. Every admin action calls a service function.

User dislikes ORM logic leaking into views: views call services, services call repositories in app/repositories, and only repositories import sqlalchemy.select. When adding a feature, add repository functions with explicit names (list_pending_for_export) rather than generic query builders.

Every mutating RPC requires an idempotency key in gRPC metadata "idempotency-key". The unary interceptor internal/server/idempotency.go looks up idempotency_keys(key, client_id, method, request_hash, response bytea, status) inside the same transaction as the operation: same key + hash returns the stored response; same key + different hash returns codes.FailedPrecondition "idempotency key reused with different request". Keys expire after 48h via a cleanup job.

Detox tests timed out waiting for the app to become idle ("The app is busy with the following tasks: Run loop 'Main Run Loop' is awake ... Network requests") because the map screen keeps fetching tiles. Fix: on the map screens in E2E builds we set DETOX_DISABLE_MAP_TILES via react-native-config to render a placeholder, and use device.disableSynchronization() only around the recording timer test.

Two-way conflicts (file changed locally and remotely since last sync) are not merged. `fsync pull` writes the remote copy as name.fsync-conflict-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.ext next to the local file and reports the conflict; `push` refuses to overwrite a remote object whose ETag differs from the manifest's unless --overwrite-remote. Decided to keep fsync one-directional per command instead of a bidirectional sync engine.

Under load test: "failed to connect to `host=paygate-db user=paygate database=paygate`: server error (FATAL: sorry, too many clients already (SQLSTATE 53300))". 8 pods x pgxpool default max_conns (4 x NumCPU = 32 on 8-core nodes) exceeded max_connections 200. Fix: pool_max_conns=15 in DATABASE_URL and pool_max_conn_idle_time=5m; no PgBouncer in front of paygate (we use LISTEN in the outbox relay).

Celery queues and routing (task_routes in app/celery_config.py): default (reservations, flags, cache warmers), emails (all app.tasks.emails.*), fulfillment (Kestrel export, capture, tracking sync). Each queue has its own worker Deployment so a backlog of emails cannot delay payment capture. prefetch_multiplier=1 and acks_late=True on all workers because tasks are long and must not be lost on pod eviction.

Catalog model: products (name, slug, brand, description) has many product_variants (sku unique, size, color, price_cents, weight_grams, is_active). Inventory, cart_items and order_items reference variant_id, never product_id. order_items snapshots sku, name and unit_price_cents at purchase time so later catalog edits do not change past orders.

Configuration is a pydantic-settings Settings class in app/settings.py reading env vars and .env (see .env.example). Required secrets (DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) have no defaults so the app fails at startup if missing. Locally STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_xxx; never commit .env.

Payment events on paygate.payment-events.v1 are protobuf-encoded (proto/paygate/events/v1/events.proto: PaymentAuthorized, PaymentCaptured, PaymentRefunded, PaymentFailed), not JSON, and registered in the Confluent-compatible schema registry with subject naming TopicNameStrategy and compatibility BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE. Chose protobuf to share types with the gRPC API and get buf breaking checks on event schemas too. Consumers (ledgerflow ingestion, shopfront is not a consumer) must tolerate unknown fields. Each event carries event_id (UUIDv7), payment_id, occurred_at and a sequence number per payment so consumers can drop out-of-order duplicates.

i18n uses Flask-Babel 4 with locales de (default), en, fr. Strings are extracted with `pybabel extract -F babel.cfg -o messages.pot .` and translations live in app/translations/<lang>/LC_MESSAGES/messages.po. Locale selection: URL prefix /en, /fr, otherwise de. Prices are formatted with babel.numbers.format_currency per locale.

dbt/profiles.yml targets: dev (each developer's schema DBT_<initials>, warehouse DEV_WH, authenticator externalbrowser), ci, prod (role TRANSFORMER, key-pair). Use `dbt build -s +my_model --target dev` locally; dev runs against a 10% sampled copy of RAW (RAW_SAMPLE) via the source() override macro when target.name == 'dev'.

Large syncs against S3 started failing with "SlowDown: Please reduce your request rate." (HTTP 503) at ~3,500 PUTs/s on a single prefix. The SDK's standard retry mode gave up after 3 attempts. Fix: RetryConfig::adaptive().with_max_attempts(10) and a client-side token bucket (governor crate) defaulting to 2000 requests/s, configurable as [limits] requests_per_second.

Integration tests in internal/store use testcontainers-go with postgres:16-alpine, apply migrations (golang-migrate files in migrations/) once per package in TestMain, and give each test its own schema via search_path. Run `go test ./... -tags=integration`; requires Docker. Unit tests use the fake acquirer and a sqlc Querier mock generated with mockery.

Payments stuck in status authorizing after client cancellations: the handler passed the request ctx to the acquirer call and to the DB update, so when the client canceled, the acquirer authorization went through but the UPDATE failed with "context canceled". Fix: after sending to the acquirer, the remaining work uses context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (Go 1.21+) with its own 10s timeout. A reconciler job (cmd/reconcile) resolves any payment in authorizing older than 5 min by querying the acquirer.

Coupon codes are case-insensitive via a citext column coupons.code. The migration failed in CI with "psycopg.errors.UndefinedObject: type "citext" does not exist". Fix: op.execute("CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS citext") at the top of the migration; the shopfront_template DB in tests also needs it.

Evaluated S3 Express One Zone directory buckets (2026-09) for a user with millions of small files. Findings: directory buckets require CreateSession-based auth (the SDK handles it transparently in aws-sdk-s3 >= 1.30), keys must not contain "//", ListObjectsV2 returns results unordered, and custom metadata works but storage classes do not. ferrosync's diff assumed sorted listings for --verify-remote, which broke.

Decision: support is not planned before v1.0. The client detects --x-s3 bucket name suffix and exits with "S3 Express directory buckets are not supported yet" (exit code 2) instead of producing a wrong plan. If we add support, --verify-remote must collect the listing into a BTreeMap before diffing (memory cost ~200 bytes per key) and storage_class must be ignored.

Payment states: created -> authorizing -> authorized -> capturing -> captured, with void from authorized, refunded/partially_refunded from captured, failed from authorizing/capturing. Transitions in internal/service/state.go use UPDATE payments SET status=$new WHERE id=$id AND status=$expected; zero rows affected returns ErrInvalidState (optimistic concurrency, no FOR UPDATE).

Dockerfile is multi-stage: node:20-alpine builds assets, python:3.12-slim builds wheels with uv pip compile from requirements/base.in, final stage python:3.12-slim with a non-root user app (uid 10001). Image is ~210MB. Same image runs web and workers; the command differs per Deployment.

ingress-nginx 4.10 behind an AWS NLB (service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: external, nlb-target-type: ip). Proxy protocol enabled on the NLB and use-proxy-protocol: "true" in the controller ConfigMap so real client IPs reach apps (shopfront's ProxyFix relies on X-Forwarded-For). Global settings: proxy-body-size 20m, keep-alive 75.

Atlantis setup: runs in the platform cluster namespace atlantis as a StatefulSet (1 replica, 50Gi PVC for plan files), version 0.28, GitHub app integration. It assumes the role atlantis-terraform in each AWS account via IRSA + role chaining (prod and staging accounts are separate). repos.yaml (server-side) forbids custom workflows from the repo except our approved ones and requires `approved` and `mergeable` before apply. Apply locks are per project (root dir), so two PRs can apply different roots at once.

Workflow customisations: the default workflow runs `terraform init -input=false`, `terraform plan -lock-timeout=5m`, plus a `tflint --recursive` and `checkov -d . --quiet --framework terraform` step that comment results but do not block. Plans for prod roots also post an infracost diff. Atlantis does not run on changes to k8s/ — those go through ArgoCD.

API request/response schemas use pydantic v2 (app/api/schemas/*.py) instead of marshmallow. Chose pydantic for speed and because services already used dataclasses with type hints. ORM objects are converted with Model.model_validate(obj) and model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True).

DNS: Route53 public zone example.test and private zone internal.example.test, managed by external-dns 0.14 with policy upsert-only (never deletes records) and txtOwnerId per cluster (prod-eu1, staging-eu1) so two clusters never fight over records.

Error design in ferrosync-core: CoreError is an enum with variants Io { path, source }, Manifest(ManifestError), Remote(S3Error), Guard(GuardViolation), Conflict { path }. Every variant that concerns a file carries the RelPath so the CLI can print "upload failed: photos/2024/img_001.heic: connection reset". S3Error wraps SdkError and exposes is_retryable() and code() (the S3 error code string like "SlowDown"); the CLI maps codes to hints (AccessDenied -> "check IAM policy, see docs/iam-policy.json"). Do not use anyhow::Error inside core; convert at the CLI boundary with .context(). Partial failures are collected into RunReport.failures instead of aborting the run, unless the error is a Guard or a manifest error, which abort immediately.

Nightly ingest of the shopfront replica failed with "Numeric value '12,90' is not recognized" on COPY INTO. Not orders at all: the failing table was legacy_vouchers, whose amount column is TEXT with German decimal commas, and pandas inferred it as string in the Parquet file. Fix: cast in the extract query and declare the Parquet schema explicitly in dags/ingest/schemas/legacy_vouchers.py instead of inferring from pandas.

To test webhooks locally: `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:5000/webhooks/stripe` prints a whsec_test_xxx secret to put in .env as STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, then `stripe trigger payment_intent.succeeded`. Note that triggered events have no shopfront metadata.order_id, so handlers log "unknown order" and return 200; use a real checkout with card 4000002500003155 to test 3DS.

Chose blake3 over sha256 for content hashing because hashing was 60% of scan time on large photo folders; blake3 with the rayon feature hashes ~3 GB/s on an M2 vs ~400 MB/s for sha2. S3 integrity still uses the SDK's checksum (CRC32C via ChecksumAlgorithm::Crc32C) on upload; the blake3 hash is stored in object metadata x-amz-meta-fsync-blake3 for change detection.

Karpenter NodePools: general (on-demand + spot, c/m/r families gen >= 6, consolidationPolicy WhenUnderutilized), batch (spot only, taint workload=batch:NoSchedule, used by Airflow task pods via tolerations), and stateful (on-demand only, for Redis/Kafka). Spot interruptions are handled via the SQS interruption queue karpenter-prod-eu1.

Pulling a bucket created on Linux to Windows failed on keys like logs/aux.txt and "notes/what?.md" with "The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect. (os error 123)". pull now maps reserved names and characters <>:"|?* to a percent-encoded form (aux%2Etxt) on Windows and records the mapping in the manifest so push maps them back.

E2E tests use Detox 20 with Jest circus in e2e/. Configurations: ios.sim.debug (iPhone 15, iOS 17.5) and android.emu.debug (Pixel_7_API_34 AVD). Location is mocked with `xcrun simctl location booted start --speed=1.5 e2e/fixtures/loop.gpx` driven from e2e/helpers/location.ts. Run `yarn detox build -c ios.sim.debug && yarn detox test -c ios.sim.debug`.

Creating orders occasionally raised "psycopg.errors.UniqueViolation: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "ix_orders_public_number"". With a 5-char suffix per day collisions happen after a few thousand orders/day. generate_order_number now retries up to 5 times on IntegrityError inside a SAVEPOINT (session.begin_nested()).

Multipart threshold is 64 MiB with 16 MiB parts (configurable via [upload] part_size). Below the threshold a single PutObject is used. Chose 16 MiB parts because S3's 10,000 part limit then allows files up to ~156 GiB; for larger files part_size is auto-raised to ceil(size/9000) rounded up to 1 MiB.

Sentry is initialised in app/observability.py with the DSN from SENTRY_DSN, traces_sample_rate=0.05 for web and 0.01 for Celery, and a before_send hook that strips card fields and the Authorization header. The Celery integration is enabled; set SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT=staging|production per Helm values.

Interceptor chain (cmd/paygate/main.go, grpc.ChainUnaryInterceptor): recovery (grpc-ecosystem/go-grpc-middleware/v2 recovery) -> otelgrpc stats handler (not an interceptor, set via grpc.StatsHandler) -> logging (slog) -> auth (mTLS client cert to client_id) -> ratelimit (per client_id token bucket) -> idempotency -> validation (protovalidate). Order matters: idempotency must run after auth because keys are scoped per client_id.

Transactional emails are Celery tasks in app/tasks/emails.py (send_order_confirmation, send_shipping_notification, send_password_reset) routed to the emails queue. They render templates from app/templates/email/*.html (compiled from MJML sources in assets/email/*.mjml with `npm run build:email`) and send via SMTP; locally mailpit catches everything on port 1025.

shopfront sells in EUR only. There is no currency column on orders; payments.currency exists but is always "eur" because Stripe requires it. Multi-currency was explicitly descoped in the 2026 roadmap; do not add currency handling unless asked.

A user on a VM with a drifting clock got "RequestTimeTooSkewed: The difference between the request time and the current time is too large." on every request. aws-sdk-s3 does not auto-correct skew. fsync doctor now reports skew, and the error message in ferrosync-s3 maps this code to "your system clock is off by Ns; sync it (e.g. with chronyd/ntp)".

Issue #88 (v0.4.2): `fsync push --delete` on /Volumes/Photos while the drive was not mounted saw an empty directory and planned deletion of 41,203 objects. The run was stopped by the user after ~6,000 deletes; versioning was enabled on that bucket so objects were restored with a script listing delete markers (ListObjectVersions) and removing them.

Fixes shipped in 0.4.3: (1) the delete-ratio guard (refuse > 20% / > 1000 objects without --max-delete); (2) the sync root must contain .ferrosync/manifest.db whose meta.root_id matches the bucket's s3://bucket/prefix/.ferrosync-root marker, otherwise fsync refuses with "sync root does not match remote (missing .ferrosync marker)"; (3) `fsync plan` prints the delete count prominently in red. We also recommend bucket versioning in the README for any bucket used with --delete.

SDK timeouts configured in crates/ferrosync-s3/src/client.rs: connect 3s, operation attempt timeout 120s for UploadPart, 30s for other calls, overall operation timeout 10 min. These are TimeoutConfig values; --timeout-scale 2.0 multiplies all of them for slow links.

Exit codes (documented in docs/exit-codes.md): 0 success, 1 generic error, 2 usage error (clap), 3 partial failure (some actions failed, details in summary), 4 refused by safety guard (delete ratio, root marker mismatch), 5 lock held by another run. Scripts rely on 3 vs 1, so do not collapse them.

Chose astronomer-cosmos over a single BashOperator running `dbt build` because a failure in one model used to fail the whole 40-minute run and retries re-ran everything. Cosmos renders the manifest into per-model tasks; we use LoadMode.DBT_MANIFEST with a manifest.json built in CI so DAG parsing does not call dbt ls (parsing took 90s otherwise).

Celery chords and groups with result collection are not used in shopfront: with no result backend (task_ignore_result) chords fail with "NotImplementedError: Starting chords requires a result backend to be configured". Fan-out work like nightly sitemap rebuilds is done by a parent task that enqueues children and a separate completion check, instead of enabling a Redis result backend.

Monthly AWS cost (October 2026): ~14.2k EUR, of which EC2 6.1k (after Karpenter spot), RDS 3.4k, NAT gateways 1.1k, S3 0.8k. NAT cost is high because nodes pull images from ghcr.io through NAT; open ticket INFRA-219 to add a pull-through cache in ECR.

Snowflake warehouses: TRANSFORM_WH (Medium) for dbt, LOAD_WH (X-Small) for COPY INTO, BI_WH (Small, auto-suspend 60s) for Metabase. Moved dbt from Large to Medium in 2026-06: run time went from 21 to 28 min but credits dropped 45%. fct_order_items full refreshes use a temporary override snowflake_warehouse='TRANSFORM_L_WH' in the model config.

Partial refunds: Refund RPC accepts amount_minor <= captured - already refunded; multiple partial refunds allowed until fully refunded. The check runs inside the transaction using SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the payment row (one of few places with pessimistic locking, because concurrent partial refunds could otherwise exceed the captured amount).

Celery beat schedule is defined in app/celery_config.py beat_schedule: release_expired_reservations every 60s, flag_expiring_authorizations hourly, send_abandoned_cart_emails every 30 min, export_orders_to_kestrel at 01:30 Europe/Berlin, rebuild_sitemaps at 03:00. Beat runs as a single-replica Deployment shopfront-beat with the redbeat scheduler so restarts do not double-fire.

Celery task retry convention: @celery.task(bind=True, autoretry_for=(httpx.TransportError, ParcelHubUnavailable), retry_backoff=5, retry_backoff_max=600, retry_jitter=True, max_retries=8). Never retry on stripe.error.CardError or validation errors. Tasks must be idempotent because acks_late=True is set globally.

POST /checkout/confirm and POST /api/v1/orders require an Idempotency-Key header (the storefront form sends a hidden uuid4). Keys are stored in idempotency_keys(key, customer_id, request_hash, response_json, created_at) for 24h. Same key + same request hash returns the stored response; same key + different hash returns 422.

All timestamps in MARTS are TIMESTAMP_NTZ in UTC; business reporting dates (order_date_berlin) are derived columns computed with convert_timezone('UTC', 'Europe/Berlin', created_at)::date. Decided after revenue per day differed from shopfront's admin dashboard, which uses Berlin days.

Checkout shipping step intermittently hung for 30s and then Gunicorn killed the worker ("WORKER TIMEOUT (pid:42)"). ParcelHub /rates sometimes takes >25s. Fix: httpx client in app/integrations/parcelhub.py with timeout=httpx.Timeout(4.0, connect=2.0), and on timeout fall back to the flat-rate table shipping_fallback_rates (DE 4.90, EU 9.90).

`flask seed-db --size small|medium|large` creates fake catalog and customers with Faker (seed 1337): small = 200 variants/50 customers, large = 20k variants/5k customers/50k orders for EXPLAIN work. It refuses to run if DATABASE_URL host is not localhost or postgres. Admin login after seeding: admin@shopfront.test / devpassword.

Chose Karpenter (v0.37, NodePool/EC2NodeClass APIs) over Cluster Autoscaler with managed node groups because we run mixed workloads (Airflow KubernetesExecutor pods spike to 200 pods at 04:00) and Karpenter's bin packing and spot diversification cut EC2 cost ~35%. One small managed node group (2x m6i.large, on-demand) hosts Karpenter itself and CoreDNS.

Airflow 2.8 -> 2.9 upgrade notes (done on staging 2026-09-02, prod 2026-09-09):
- Helm chart 1.12 -> 1.13; migrations ran via the chart's migrateDatabaseJob (took 3 minutes on the 40 GB metadata DB; we ran `airflow db clean --clean-before-timestamp 2026-06-01` first to cut it from 9 minutes).
- Datasets UI changed; dataset-triggered DAG runs now show the triggering events.
- The Cosmos version had to go to 1.4 for 2.9 compatibility; 1.3 failed with "ImportError: cannot import name 'DbtDag'" style errors due to a changed import path.
- Our custom S3ToSnowflake operator used airflow.providers.amazon BaseOperator imports that were removed; rewrote to use S3Hook directly.
- Pinned constraints file constraints-3.11.txt for 2.9.3 in the image Dockerfile; never pip install providers without constraints (broke the scheduler once with a newer SQLAlchemy).

Erased (GDPR) customers kept appearing as current in dim_customers. The snapshot did not track deletes and the source keeps erased rows but anonymized. Added invalidate_hard_deletes=True and a filter in dim_customers: where erased_at is null for the "active" flag; GDPR-erased rows in snapshots are anonymized by the weekly gdpr_scrub DAG that updates SNAPSHOTS.snap_customers in place.

iOS stopped recording after ~10 minutes with the screen locked. The LocationRecorder used CLLocationManager without allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates = true and showsBackgroundLocationIndicator; also UIBackgroundModes "location" was missing from Info.plist in the Release config only (it was set in a Debug-only plist override). Fixed both; pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically = false while recording.

--bwlimit design: a shared governor RateLimiter keyed on bytes, with each part reader acquiring permits in 64 KiB chunks before handing data to the SDK body stream (ByteStream from a custom http_body::Body). Chose throttling at the reader rather than a custom hyper connector because the SDK's connector API changes too often. Known issue: SDK buffers up to the part size in some retry paths, causing bursts.

Sitemaps are rebuilt nightly at 03:00 by rebuild_sitemaps into the media bucket under sitemaps/sitemap-products-{n}.xml (45k URLs per file) plus sitemap-index.xml; /sitemap.xml redirects to the bucket URL. Only active variants' parent products and categories are included.

Recording uses distanceFilter 10 m and desiredAccuracy kCLLocationAccuracyBest on iOS / PRIORITY_HIGH_ACCURACY with 2s interval on Android. We considered adaptive accuracy based on speed but dropped it after field tests: battery saving was ~8%/hour vs ~11%/hour, not worth the jagged tracks. Revisit only with user complaints.

Refunds: app/services/refunds.py:create_refund creates a refunds row (status pending), calls stripe.Refund.create with amount in cents and metadata.refund_id, and the charge.refund.updated webhook flips it to succeeded/failed. Partial refunds are allowed per order_item; the sum of refunds may never exceed payments.captured_cents (checked in a DB CHECK via trigger).

dbt run of fct_orders failed with "100090 (42P18): Duplicate row detected during DML action Row Values: [...]". The incremental batch contained the same order_id twice because stg_shopfront__orders unioned two replica extracts during a cutover. Fix: dedupe in the staging model with qualify row_number() over (partition by order_id order by _loaded_at desc) = 1, and a unique test on stg_shopfront__orders.order_id.

SCD2 history of customers and product prices uses dbt snapshots in dbt/snapshots/ (snap_customers, snap_variant_prices) with strategy='timestamp', updated_at='updated_at', target schema SNAPSHOTS. dim_customers is built from snap_customers with dbt_valid_from/dbt_valid_to. Snapshots run in their own task group before marts.

Android 14 crash on starting a recording: "java.lang.SecurityException: Starting FGS with type location callerApp=... targetSDK=34 requires permissions: all of the permissions allOf=true [android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION]". Fix: add <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION"/> and android:foregroundServiceType="location" on the service in AndroidManifest.xml, and request ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION before starting the service.

shopfront architecture as of 2026-09: a single Flask 3.0 app (app/__init__.py create_app factory) serving three blueprints: storefront (Jinja + HTMX), api (JSON for the mobile client, /api/v1), and admin (HTMX, behind Flask-Login with is_staff). Data lives in Postgres 15 accessed through SQLAlchemy 2.0 with Alembic migrations in migrations/versions. Background work runs on Celery 5.3 with Redis 7 as the broker; there is no result backend (task_ignore_result=True globally).

Layering convention: views -> app/services/*.py (business logic, no Flask imports) -> app/repositories/*.py (all SQLAlchemy queries). Services receive a Session explicitly; they never touch flask.g. Payments go through Stripe PaymentIntents (app/services/payments.py), shipping quotes through the ParcelHub sandbox API (app/integrations/parcelhub.py), and fulfillment to the Kestrel Logistics warehouse via nightly SFTP plus an inbound webhook.

Main tables: customers, products, product_variants (one sku per variant), inventory (variant_id, on_hand, reserved), inventory_reservations, carts, cart_items, orders, order_items, payments, refunds, shipments, coupons, processed_events. All money columns are integer cents (BIGINT) in EUR. Everything is deployed as two images (web, worker) via the Helm chart in deploy/helm/shopfront.

TanStack Query cache is persisted to MMKV for offline viewing of saved trails using @tanstack/query-sync-storage-persister with throttleTime 2000 and maxAge 7 days; only queries with meta.persist = true are dehydrated (shouldDehydrateQuery). Offline mutations (saving a hike) are queued via onlineManager and resumePausedMutations on reconnect.

mypy started failing after the SQLAlchemy 2.0 conversion of orders.py with "error: Incompatible return value type (got "Sequence[Order]", expected "list[Order]")". session.scalars(...).all() returns Sequence. Convention: repository functions return Sequence[...] (from collections.abc) instead of list[...], callers that need a list call list() explicitly.

`flask db upgrade` failed with "alembic.util.exc.CommandError: Multiple head revisions are present for given argument 'head'" after two feature branches each added a migration off the same parent. Fix: `flask db merge -m "merge heads" <rev1> <rev2>`, commit the empty merge revision. CI now runs `flask db heads | wc -l` and fails if more than one.

Cargo features: ferrosync-s3 has integration (enables tests against MinIO), rustls-ring (default), native-tls (for corporate proxies with custom CAs). The CLI exposes --ca-bundle path which works with both TLS backends; HTTPS_PROXY is respected through the SDK's hyper client.

Symlinks are not followed by default; they are skipped with a warning listing the count at the end of a run. --follow-symlinks follows them with loop detection via (dev, inode) set. We decided not to upload symlinks as special objects (like rclone's .rclonelink) because restoring them cross-platform was a support burden in other tools.

Stripe API version upgrade 2022-11-15 -> 2024-06-20 (done 2026-07):

Why now: the old version returned charges inline on PaymentIntent (payment_intent.charges.data[0]) which the new SDK (stripe-python 10.x) no longer types; we needed latest_charge for the dispute flow, and automatic_payment_methods became the default.

How we did it: pinned stripe.api_version = "2024-06-20" explicitly in app/services/payments.py rather than relying on the account default, created a second webhook endpoint with the new version in the dashboard pointing at /webhooks/stripe?v=2 for two weeks while the handler accepted both payload shapes (checking event.api_version), then removed the old endpoint. Code changes: replaced intent.charges.data[0] with stripe.Charge.retrieve(intent.latest_charge) where needed (refunds and disputes only), removed payment_method_types=["card"] in favour of automatic_payment_methods={"enabled": True}, and updated stripe-mock to v0.186 which supports the new version. Lesson: the webhook endpoint's version is set in the dashboard per endpoint and is independent of the API version used by our requests.

Recorded hikes upload as GPX-like JSON (points as [lat, lon, ts, accuracy]) gzip-compressed with pako to POST /v2/hikes; points over 50k are split into chunks with PUT /v2/hikes/<id>/points?chunk=n. Upload retries with exponential backoff up to 24h while the hike is marked pending in op-sqlite.

Local development setup for paygate: `make dev` runs docker compose with postgres:16 (port 5434), redpanda as Kafka (9092, console on 8082), the schema registry built into redpanda, and an otel-collector with a debug exporter. `make migrate` applies migrations/ with golang-migrate, `make run` starts cmd/paygate with ACQUIRER=fake and mTLS disabled via DEV_INSECURE=1 (refuses to start if APP_ENV=production). grpcurl calls use -plaintext against :9090 with metadata -H 'idempotency-key: <uuid>' -H 'x-dev-client-id: shopfront'. The fake acquirer declines amounts ending in 05 with code 05 and times out for amounts ending in 99, which tests and manual checks rely on.

Retries of UploadPart failed with "StreamingBody cannot be retried: body is not rewindable" when the part body came from a custom streaming reader. The SDK can only retry bodies it can re-create. Fix: parts are created with ByteStream::read_from().path(...).offset(o).length(Length::Exact(n)) which is rewindable; the bwlimit reader wraps a file-backed SdkBody built with SdkBody::retryable.

Bumping the AWS provider from 5.30 to 5.45 produced "Error: Unsupported argument: An argument named "enable_classiclink" is not expected here" in an old pinned VPC module version used by staging/network. Upgrade the community vpc module to 5.8 at the same time and run `terraform init -upgrade`; read the module's UPGRADE.md for removed variables.

As of 2026-10-28 the migration of billing models from the old Python ETL (etl/legacy_billing.py run by cron) to dbt is about 60% done: stg_billing__invoices, stg_billing__payments and fct_invoices are live; fct_mrr and dim_subscriptions still come from the legacy job writing to LEGACY.BILLING_MRR. Plan: parallel run for two weeks comparing fct_mrr against LEGACY.BILLING_MRR with an audit_helper compare_relations test before switching Metabase.

Load tests live in loadtest/locustfile.py with users StorefrontBrowser, CartUser and CheckoutUser. Run against staging with `locust -f loadtest/locustfile.py --host https://staging.shopfront.test -u 600 -r 20 --run-time 15m --headless --csv loadtest/out/run`. CheckoutUser uses Stripe test card 4242424242424242 and needs LOADTEST_API_TOKEN.

Upload of a 70 MiB file failed with "EntityTooSmall: Your proposed upload is smaller than the minimum allowed size" from CompleteMultipartUpload. A bug in the part splitter produced a 5 MiB-minus-1 part in the middle when part_size was not a multiple of the read buffer. Fixed in crates/ferrosync-s3/src/multipart.rs by computing part boundaries from the file size up front (only the last part may be < 5 MiB); proptest added in tests/multipart_props.rs.

Changing the shopfront RDS instance class in Terraform showed "apply_immediately = false" and nothing happened for days. Changes wait for the maintenance window (Sun 03:00-04:00 UTC). For urgent resizes set apply_immediately = true in the PR, apply, then revert the flag in a follow-up PR so later changes do not trigger surprise reboots.

Request validation uses protovalidate-go with buf.validate annotations in the .proto files (e.g. amount_minor gt 0, currency len 3, merchant_id uuid) instead of hand-written checks or protoc-gen-validate, which is in maintenance mode. Business rules that need DB state stay in internal/service.

tests/services/test_reservations.py::test_expired_reservation_released failed only between 22:00 and 24:00 locally. Cause: expires_at compared against datetime.now() (naive local time) while the DB stores timestamptz in UTC. Fixed by using app.clock.utcnow() everywhere and freezegun's freeze_time("2026-03-01T12:00:00Z") in the test.

Scheduler logs showed "airflow.exceptions.AirflowTaskTimeout: DagBag import timeout for /opt/airflow/dags/dbt_daily.py after 30.0s" and the DAG disappeared from the UI. Cosmos was using LoadMode.DBT_LS. Fix: switched to LoadMode.DBT_MANIFEST with dbt/target/manifest.json baked into the image, and raised dagbag_import_timeout to 60 as a safety margin.

Metrics: Prometheus via otel metrics exporter on :9464/metrics; key metrics paygate_authorize_duration_seconds (histogram by acquirer_code), outbox_oldest_age_seconds, ledger_unbalanced_total (should always be 0). Traces go to the OTel collector at otel-collector.observability:4317. Logs are slog JSON with trace_id and payment_id attributes.

Incident 2026-08-18: Airflow task pods stayed Pending for 25 minutes at 04:00 and dbt_daily missed its SLA. Karpenter logs: "could not schedule pod, incompatible with nodepool "batch", daemonset overhead={...} no instance type satisfied resources {"cpu":"8","memory":"34Gi"} and requirements karpenter.sh/capacity-type In [spot]". A dbt task pod requested 34Gi (a typo in the Cosmos pod_override: 34Gi instead of 4Gi) and spot capacity for big memory instances in the allowed families was unavailable; Karpenter kept retrying that pod, and the other pending pods queued behind the DAG's concurrency limit.

Fixes: the ledgerflow pod_override was corrected; the batch NodePool now allows on-demand as a fallback (capacity-type In [spot, on-demand] with a weight preferring spot); a LimitRange in the airflow namespace caps container memory at 8Gi so such typos fail fast with a clear admission error.

All timestamp columns are TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE and Python code uses timezone-aware UTC datetimes via app/clock.py (utcnow(), which tests can patch). Conversion to Europe/Berlin happens only for display and for the beat schedule. A ruff rule (DTZ) is enabled to forbid naive datetime.now().

Log pipeline: OTel collector DaemonSet (opentelemetry-collector-contrib 0.98) with the filelog receiver reading /var/log/pods, k8sattributes processor adding namespace/pod/app labels, a transform processor that parses JSON bodies (shopfront structlog, paygate slog) into attributes, and the loki exporter to Loki 3 with labels limited to namespace, app, container and level to keep cardinality low (request_id and payment_id stay in the log line and are queried with | json). A filter processor drops kube-probe health check access logs from ingress-nginx, which were 30% of volume. Retention 30 days via the Loki compactor; S3 bucket example-loki-chunks with lifecycle to IA after 7 days. Per-tenant ingestion limit 20 MB/s; Airflow task logs go to S3 remote logging directly, not through Loki, because of their size.

Persistence uses react-native-mmkv 2.12 with two instances: "settings" (unencrypted: units, map style) and "secure" (encryptionKey from react-native-keychain, holds the refresh token). Zustand persist middleware uses a custom createJSONStorage adapter around the settings instance in src/stores/storage.ts.

For local cross-compilation (e.g. aarch64-unknown-linux-musl from a Mac), use `cross build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` with cross 0.2.5 and Docker running. Cross.toml pins the image ghcr.io/cross-rs/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl:0.2.5. Release builds in CI do not use cross; cargo-dist uses native runners.

HTMX convention: full pages extend templates/base.html; partials live next to their page under templates/<area>/_partials/_name.html and are returned when request.headers.get("HX-Request") is set (helper app/htmx.py:render_page_or_partial). Server-sent errors use HX-Retarget to #flash and a 422 status.

Library tab with 400+ recorded hikes scrolled at ~20 fps on mid-range Android. FlatList rendered a static map thumbnail (Mapbox Static Images API) and computed formatted distances in each row render. Replaced FlatList with @shopify/flash-list 1.7 (estimatedItemSize 96), memoized rows with React.memo and a stable keyExtractor, moved formatting to the query select function, and cached thumbnails with expo-image (cachePolicy 'disk'). Now ~58 fps on a Pixel 6a; measured with the Flashlight tool (flashlight measure) as user prefers numbers over impressions.

On upload ferrosync sets object metadata x-amz-meta-fsync-mtime (unix ns), x-amz-meta-fsync-blake3 (hex) and x-amz-meta-fsync-mode (unix permission bits, octal). Metadata values must be ASCII; non-ASCII original filenames are never stored in metadata, only in the key.

Builds and store submission use EAS Build/Submit (eas.json profiles development, preview, production) even though the app is bare RN; we dropped Fastlane in 2026-03 because maintaining match certificates on CI was painful. Versioning uses appVersionSource "remote" so EAS auto-increments buildNumber/versionCode.

Product images go to an S3-compatible bucket (MinIO locally at http://localhost:9000, bucket shopfront-media, keys minioadmin/minioadmin) and to the cloud bucket in prod. The admin uploads via presigned PUT URLs generated in app/services/media.py with a 10 minute expiry; the browser uploads directly, then the admin form posts the key.

Flask-SQLAlchemy is still installed only because app/admin and app/repositories/carts.py use Model.query. app/db.py already defines engine, SessionLocal (sessionmaker, expire_on_commit=False) and session_scope(); the request session is created in a before_request hook and removed in teardown_appcontext. Dropping Flask-SQLAlchemy is blocked on the SQLAlchemy 2.0 migration of admin.

Daily reconciliation flagged ~200 mismatches on 2026-08-01: amounts differed by exactly the fee. The acquirer changed the settlement file to report net amounts (column NET_AMT) instead of gross from August. Parser internal/reconcile/settlement.go now reads the file version header (v2 = net) and compares against captured amount minus fees:acquirer ledger entries.

User wants golangci-lint (config .golangci.yml: errcheck, govet, staticcheck, gosec, errorlint, wrapcheck, revive) clean before commit, errors wrapped with fmt.Errorf("authorize payment %s: %w", id, err), and no naked returns. Table-driven tests with t.Run and testify/require only (no assert).

order_events table records every state transition (order_id, from_status, to_status, event, actor_type staff|customer|system|webhook, actor_id, created_at, payload jsonb). The admin order page renders it as a timeline. It is append-only; a trigger rejects UPDATE and DELETE.

Cloudflare R2-compatible endpoints work with endpoint_url = "https://<account>.r2.example.test" and region = "auto". R2 does not support ChecksumAlgorithm::Crc32C on multipart (returns NotImplemented), so profiles with r2 = true (or detected by host suffix) disable flexible checksums and rely on Content-MD5 per part.

Deletes are opt-in: by default fsync only uploads. --delete removes remote objects whose local files are gone, but refuses if the plan would delete more than 20% of remote objects or more than 1000 objects unless --max-delete N or --force-delete is given. Added after a user synced an unmounted (empty) external drive folder and nearly wiped a bucket in v0.4 testing.

Flask-WTF CSRFProtect is enabled app-wide. The webhooks blueprint (app/webhooks/: stripe.py, kestrel.py) is exempted with csrf.exempt(webhooks_bp) in create_app; the api blueprint is also exempt because it authenticates with bearer tokens, not cookies. Admin and storefront forms must include {{ csrf_token() }}.

Deploy stuck with the shopfront-migrate hook Job in BackoffLimitExceeded; logs showed "psycopg.errors.LockNotAvailable: canceling statement due to lock timeout" on ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN. Long-running admin report queries held AccessShareLock. Migrations set lock_timeout='5s' (env.py); fix was to retry outside business hours. Convention: add columns nullable without default, backfill in batches in a Celery task, then add NOT NULL in a later migration.

Undefined symbols for architecture arm64: _OBJC_CLASS_$_SkiaManager". Cause: stale pods. When the bundle behaves oddly after dependency changes: `yarn start --reset-cache`, `watchman watch-del-all`, delete ios/build and android/app/build. Metro config (metro.config.js) adds .cjs to sourceExts for the TanStack packages and enables unstable_enablePackageExports=false because some packages break with exports resolution.

ArgoCD 2.11 app-of-apps: k8s/argocd/apps/<env>/*.yaml Applications, auto-sync with prune and selfHeal for platform apps; app teams' Applications have automated sync but selfHeal false for shopfront (it wants manual rollback decisions). Image tags are bumped by CI in the app repos via a PR to infra-live changing values-<env>.yaml image.tag; ArgoCD Image Updater is not used.

Incident 2026-03-17: a deploy renamed orders.shipping_method to orders.shipping_option in a single Alembic migration. The pre-upgrade migrate Job ran, new pods started, then readiness failed on an unrelated Redis config error and ArgoCD rolled back to the previous image. The old pods queried orders.shipping_method, which no longer existed: "psycopg.errors.UndefinedColumn: column orders.shipping_method does not exist". Checkout was down for 19 minutes until we ran the downgrade by hand from a debug pod.

Lesson and convention since then (expand/contract): every migration must be compatible with the currently deployed code. Renames are done in three deploys: (1) add the new column and write to both, backfill in batches; (2) switch reads to the new column; (3) drop the old column in a later release. Dropping columns or tables is never in the same release as the code change that stops using them. Reviewers check this with the "migration safety" section of the PR template.

Also added: ArgoCD rollbacks no longer happen automatically for shopfront (syncPolicy without selfHeal on the image tag), so a human decides whether a downgrade is needed.

Makefile targets: make up (docker compose up -d), make test (pytest -x -q), make lint (ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy), make migrate (flask db upgrade), make seed (flask seed-db --size small), make beat (celery beat with redbeat), make snapshot (scripts/pull_prod_snapshot.sh, needs VPN).

CI is GitHub Actions .github/workflows/ci.yml: jobs lint (ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy app/services), test (pytest with a postgres:15 service container and redis:7), and migrations (alembic upgrade head then downgrade -1 then upgrade head on an empty DB). Test job was 14 min in May. If CI fails with "database shopfront_template is being accessed by other users", a previous step left a connection open; the fixture now terminates backends with pg_terminate_backend before cloning.

Domain errors are sentinel/typed errors in internal/service/errors.go (ErrPaymentNotFound, ErrInvalidState, ErrDeclined{Code}) mapped to gRPC status in one place, internal/server/errors.go toStatus: NotFound, FailedPrecondition, and for declines codes.Aborted with an errdetails.ErrorInfo{Reason: "CARD_DECLINED", Metadata: {"acquirer_code": "05"}}. Handlers never build status errors themselves.

Kestrel Logistics integration: nightly export_orders_to_kestrel (01:30 Berlin) writes one XML file per day (orders in status authorized, schema in docs/kestrel/order_v4.xsd) and uploads it via SFTP to sftp.kestrel-logistics.test:/inbound/shopfront/. Kestrel calls POST /webhooks/kestrel with packed/shipped events signed with HMAC-SHA256 (header X-Kestrel-Signature, secret KESTREL_WEBHOOK_SECRET). On packed we capture the PaymentIntent; on shipped we create shipments rows and email the tracking link.

Price changes are tracked in price_history (variant_id, old_price_cents, new_price_cents, changed_by, changed_at), written by app/services/catalog.py:update_price. The storefront shows a "was" price only if the variant had a higher price within the last 30 days, per the EU price indication rule; computed by repositories.prices.lowest_price_last_30_days.

Catalog cache invalidation: app/services/catalog.py calls cache.invalidate_product(product_id) after commit using SQLAlchemy after_commit session events (registered in app/cache.py), never before commit, to avoid caching stale rows read by concurrent requests. Category listing caches are not invalidated individually; they simply expire after 2 min.

Admin order search accepts a public order number (SF-...), an email, or a Stripe PaymentIntent id (pi_...). app/admin/orders.py:search dispatches on the prefix; emails use the citext column customers.email with an exact match, not ILIKE, so partial emails do not match on purpose (GDPR review asked to avoid fuzzy customer lookup).

Duplicate customer accounts (same person, two emails) are merged by ops with `flask customers merge --from 1234 --into 5678 --dry-run` (app/cli/customers.py). It re-points orders, customer_addresses, returns and order_events.actor_id to the target, deletes the source's api_tokens, merges marketing_opt_in by OR, and writes a customer_merges audit row.

Constraints learned the hard way: Stripe customers cannot be merged, so the source's Stripe customer is kept on stripe_customers with the target customer_id (one-to-many now); saved payment methods of the source therefore still work. The command refuses if either customer is erased (GDPR) or if both have open carts with a checkout in progress (reservation present). Run it outside the 01:30 Kestrel export window because the export reads customer emails for delivery notifications.

dbt layering rules in ledgerflow, enforced in CI by dbt-project-evaluator (package 0.12) with a few exceptions listed in dbt/seeds/dbt_project_evaluator_exceptions.csv:
- staging: one model per source table, named stg_<source>__<table>, only renames, casts, light cleaning (trim, lower emails, cents to integers) and dedup with qualify. No joins. Materialized as views.
- intermediate: int_<entity>_<verb> (int_orders_joined_payments, int_subscriptions_daily_spine), joins and business logic shared by several marts. Ephemeral unless referenced by more than three models, then views.
- marts: fct_ (events/transactions, one row per business event, incremental when > 10M rows) and dim_ (entities, tables). Organised by domain folder: marts/finance, marts/commerce, marts/product.
- Marts may only ref staging or intermediate models, never sources directly (the evaluator's fct_direct_join_to_source rule).
- Every model has an owner in meta (meta: {owner: "data-platform"}) and a description; models without docs fail the evaluator.
Money columns are always *_cents integers through staging and intermediate; marts add *_eur NUMERIC(18,2) columns for BI convenience and keep the cents column too.

Shutdown: on SIGTERM main.go calls grpcServer.GracefulStop() with a 25s timeout fallback to Stop(), stops the outbox relay after the last flush, and closes the pgx pool. terminationGracePeriodSeconds is 30 and a preStop sleep of 5s lets the endpoints controller remove the pod first.

Feature flags live in the feature_flags table (name, enabled, rollout_percent, updated_at) and are read through app/flags.py:is_enabled(name, customer_id=None), cached in-process for 60s. Percentage rollout hashes customer_id with the flag name. Toggle with `flask flags set checkout_v2 --percent 25`.

Abandoned cart emails: send_abandoned_cart_emails runs every 30 min and picks carts with customer email, updated_at between 4h and 28h ago, at least one item, and no abandoned_email_sent_at. It sends at most one reminder per cart and respects customers.marketing_opt_in; carts of guests without an email are skipped.

Chose sqlc over GORM and ent because queries on payments and ledger_entries are hand-tuned (FOR UPDATE, partial indexes) and we want compile-time checked SQL without an ORM. sqlc.yaml uses engine postgresql, sql_package pgx/v5, emit_interface true so the Querier can be faked. Run `make sqlc` after editing queries; generated files are committed.

Passwords are hashed with argon2-cffi (time_cost=3, memory_cost=65536, parallelism=2). Legacy bcrypt hashes from the 2023 import are verified with passlib and transparently re-hashed to argon2 on next successful login in app/services/auth.py:verify_and_upgrade.

In the production image all text showed in German even under /en. The .mo files are not committed and the Dockerfile never compiled them. Fix: RUN pybabel compile -d app/translations in the build stage of the Dockerfile; locally run `make translations`. Missing .mo files fail silently in Flask-Babel.

Export task failed with "paramiko.ssh_exception.SSHException: Server 'sftp.kestrel-logistics.test' not found in known_hosts" after Kestrel rotated their host key on 2026-03-02. Fix: update the KESTREL_KNOWN_HOSTS secret (mounted at /etc/shopfront/known_hosts) with the new ed25519 key; we use RejectPolicy deliberately, never AutoAddPolicy.

SQL style: sqlfluff 3 with dialect snowflake and templater dbt, lowercase keywords, trailing commas, CTEs named after what they contain (orders, paid_orders), final select from a CTE named final. CI runs `sqlfluff lint dbt/models --processes 4`; user wants fixes applied with sqlfluff fix rather than hand formatting.

As of 2026-11-02: version 2.6 is in TestFlight/Play internal testing with offline packs v1 and the new elevation profile chart (victory-native XL). Blocking for release: Android 14 FGS permission prompt copy needs legal review, and the offline pack size estimate is off by ~30% for steep terrain.

The mobile API is versioned in the URL (/api/v1) and v1 must stay backward compatible because old app versions stay installed for months. Additive fields only; for breaking changes add /api/v2 routes alongside. The X-App-Version header is logged and the minimum supported version is enforced by /api/v1/config returning min_version.

The x86_64-unknown-linux-musl build failed in cargo-dist with "failed to run custom build command for `aws-lc-sys v0.17.0` ... CMake not found". aws-sdk-s3's default rustls uses aws-lc-rs. We switched the HTTP client to rustls with the ring provider via aws-smithy-runtime features to avoid needing CMake and a C toolchain for musl; builds are also faster.

Integration tests use stripe-mock (docker image stripe/stripe-mock:v0.186.0 on port 12111), configured by setting stripe.api_base in tests/conftest.py when STRIPE_MOCK=1. stripe-mock returns static fixtures and does not keep state, so tests that need a PaymentIntent to change status patch app.services.payments.retrieve_intent instead.

--verify-remote (full ListObjectsV2 of the prefix) is off by default: for a 2M-object bucket it costs 2,000 LIST requests and ~90s. Normal runs trust the manifest and only HEAD objects whose upload previously failed. Weekly `fsync verify` is recommended instead of listing on every push.

Restoring the prod snapshot into local Postgres failed with "ERROR: role "shopfront_prod" does not exist" on every ALTER ... OWNER TO line. Fix: dump with `pg_dump --no-owner --no-privileges -Fc` (or pass --no-owner to pg_restore) and restore as the local shopfront user. scripts/pull_prod_snapshot.sh now does this.

ledgerflow is the analytics pipeline: Airflow 2.9 (KubernetesExecutor, Helm chart apache-airflow 1.13 in namespace airflow) orchestrates ingestion and dbt 1.8 (dbt-snowflake 1.8) transforms in Snowflake. Ingestion: Fivetran-like extraction is done by our own Python operators in dags/ingest/ that copy Postgres replicas (shopfront_ro, billing_ro) to S3 as Parquet (pyarrow) and load them with COPY INTO into RAW.<source>.<table>. dbt project lives in dbt/ with layers staging (stg_<source>__<table>, views), intermediate (int_*, ephemeral or views), marts (fct_*, dim_*, tables or incremental) in schemas STAGING, INTERMEDIATE, MARTS. dbt runs inside Airflow via astronomer-cosmos 1.4 DbtTaskGroup, one Airflow task per model, so failures and retries are per model.

Daily schedule: ingest_* DAGs at 02:00 UTC, dbt_daily at 04:00 UTC triggered by Datasets (outlets on the ingest tasks), BI dashboards in Metabase read MARTS only.

New-developer setup that actually works on macOS (checked 2026-10-15): brew install libpq and add it to PATH for psql, `uv venv && uv pip sync requirements/dev.txt`, cp .env.example .env, make up, make migrate, make seed, then flask run --debug. psycopg[binary] is used locally; the Docker image uses psycopg[c]. If `make up` fails on port 5433, an old compose project is still running: docker compose -p shopfront-old down.

Admin permissions: staff users have role support, ops or admin (staff_users.role). Support can view orders and request refunds up to 100 EUR; ops can cancel orders and approve returns; only admin can edit prices and feature flags. Enforced by @require_role decorator in app/admin/auth.py.

-vv debug logs printed full presigned URLs and the x-amz-security-token query parameter. Fix: the tracing layer in crates/ferrosync-cli/src/output.rs redacts query strings for any URL containing X-Amz-Signature, and the SDK's own debug logging (aws_smithy_runtime=trace) is filtered out unless FSYNC_TRACE_SDK=1.
