Cluster bootstrap order for a new EKS cluster (used for staging-eu1 rebuild in 2026-04, documented in docs/runbooks/new-cluster.md):
1. terraform apply live/<env>/network (VPC, subnets with karpenter.sh/discovery tags, secondary CIDR, NAT).
2. terraform apply live/<env>/eks: cluster, OIDC provider, the small managed node group for system pods, EKS add-ons (vpc-cni with custom networking config, coredns, kube-proxy, ebs-csi, pod identity agent not installed), IRSA roles for platform components, Karpenter IAM + SQS interruption queue.
3. Bootstrap ArgoCD with `helm install argocd` from k8s/bootstrap/ (the only manual Helm install), then apply k8s/argocd/apps/<env>/root.yaml. From then on ArgoCD installs everything via sync waves: wave -2 CRDs (prometheus-operator, cert-manager, external-secrets), wave -1 external-secrets + ClusterSecretStore, karpenter, wave 0 cert-manager, external-dns, ingress-nginx, wave 1 monitoring and logging, wave 2 app namespaces with NetworkPolicies, wave 3 applications.
4. Point DNS: external-dns takes over records only with matching txtOwnerId; for a rebuilt cluster with the same id, delete the old cluster's TXT ownership records first or nothing gets updated.
Total time for staging rebuild: about 2.5 hours, of which 40 minutes waiting on the EKS control plane.

B2B customers can enter a VAT ID at checkout; it is validated against the fake VIES sandbox (app/integrations/vies.py) with a 3s timeout and cached for 7 days. A valid non-German EU VAT ID sets reverse_charge=true on the order and tax is 0 per line; if VIES is down, checkout proceeds with VAT charged and a note.

Every action runs inside a tracing span action{kind=upload path=... size=...}; per-part spans are at debug level. With --json, span fields are flattened into the events. Use #[instrument(skip(self, body), fields(path = %entry.path))] rather than manual span creation.

3DS / redirect payment flow: checkout creates the PaymentIntent with return_url=https://<host>/checkout/return?order=<public_number>. On return the page shows a "confirming payment" state and polls GET /checkout/status/<public_number> every 2s (max 30s) via HTMX hx-trigger="every 2s" until the webhook has moved the order to authorized or failed.

Pods stuck in ContainerCreating with "failed to assign an IP address to container: InsufficientCidrBlocks" / aws-node logs "failed to allocate a private IP address: no available IP addresses". The /22 private subnets ran out during the 04:00 Airflow spike. Fix: added a secondary CIDR 100.64.0.0/16 to the VPC with custom networking (ENIConfig per AZ, AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_CUSTOM_NETWORK_CFG=true) and enabled prefix delegation (ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION=true, WARM_PREFIX_TARGET=1).

No OTA updates (expo-updates / CodePush) for now: the recording native module changes often and a JS bundle mismatching the native code broke recording once in beta. All changes ship as store builds; the API enforces a minimum app version via GET /v2/config.

Payment methods offered (decided 2026-05 with finance): cards (incl. Apple Pay / Google Pay through Stripe's wallet support, no extra code), SEPA Direct Debit and Klarna via Stripe automatic_payment_methods. PayPal is not offered: the separate PayPal integration would bypass PaymentIntents and the manual-capture flow, and PayPal's authorization honor period (3 days) is shorter than our typical packing time.

SEPA Direct Debit is special: it is asynchronous (payment_intent.processing, then succeeded up to 5 business days later) and does not support manual capture. For SEPA orders we therefore skip capture_method=manual, the order goes to authorized on payment_intent.processing (risk accepted for orders below 300 EUR; above that, SEPA is hidden at checkout via payment_method_options), and a payment_intent.payment_failed after shipping creates an admin alert for dunning. Klarna supports manual capture with a 28-day authorization window, so it follows the card flow.

infra-live repo layout: terraform/ with modules/ (vpc, eks, rds, redis, s3-bucket, iam-irsa) and live/<env>/<stack> roots (live/prod/network, live/prod/eks, live/prod/data, same for staging), each with its own state. Terraform 1.8, AWS provider 5.x pinned with ~> 5.40 in versions.tf. State in S3 bucket example-tfstate-eu-central-1 with DynamoDB table tf-locks, key = "<env>/<stack>/terraform.tfstate". Plans and applies run through Atlantis (atlantis.yaml with one project per root, autoplan on changes to the root or its modules).

Kubernetes: EKS 1.29 clusters prod-eu1 and staging-eu1. Cluster add-ons and apps are managed by ArgoCD (app-of-apps in k8s/argocd/apps/), with platform charts in k8s/platform/: ingress-nginx, cert-manager, external-dns, external-secrets, karpenter, kube-prometheus-stack, loki, otel-collector. Application teams (shopfront, paygate, ledgerflow Airflow) have their Helm values in k8s/apps/<app>/values-<env>.yaml; images are built in their own repos.

Checkout flow (app/services/checkout.py, feature flag checkout_v2 at 100% since 2026-10-20):
1. POST /checkout/start: validate cart, reserve stock (reserve_stock with FOR UPDATE), create order in draft with snapshotted order_items, compute tax per line and shipping (ParcelHub quote or fallback).
2. POST /checkout/address: store shipping/billing on orders, recompute shipping.
3. POST /checkout/confirm (Idempotency-Key required): apply coupon, transition to pending_payment, create PaymentIntent (capture_method=manual, metadata.order_id), return client_secret to Stripe Elements.
4. Browser confirms payment; 3DS may redirect to /checkout/return.
5. Webhook payment_intent.succeeded -> transition to authorized, commit inventory, enqueue confirmation email.

The old checkout v1 (single POST, synchronous charge) code in app/services/checkout_legacy.py is dead since checkout_v2 hit 100% and is scheduled for deletion after Black Friday. Do not fix bugs in checkout_legacy.py.

CLI is clap 4 derive in crates/ferrosync-cli/src/args.rs. Subcommands: push, pull, plan, status, verify, gc, restore, doctor, completions. Global flags: --profile, --config, -v/-q, --json. Convention: every destructive subcommand has --dry-run and the plan output is identical to `fsync plan` with the same args.

Local dev: `docker compose up` starts postgres (15.6, port 5433 on the host to avoid clashing with a system Postgres), redis (6380 on host), minio (9000/9001), mailpit (8025 UI), web (flask run --debug on 5000) and worker (celery -A app.celery_app worker -Q default,emails,fulfillment -l info). The beat process is not in compose; run `make beat` when you need it.

As of 2026-11-18, coupon rules v2 (minimum order value, per-customer usage limit, category restrictions) is partially implemented: coupons.min_order_cents and coupon_redemptions table exist and are enforced; category restrictions (coupon_categories table) are migrated but not yet checked in apply_coupon. Branch feat/coupon-categories has the WIP.

Staging (staging.shopfront.test) is refreshed from an anonymized prod snapshot every Sunday by the infra CronJob; anonymization uses the same erase_customer logic in bulk mode. Stripe on staging uses test keys (sk_test_xxx) so real cards never work there; ParcelHub points at its sandbox.

Release process (since v0.8): cargo-dist 0.14 generates .github/workflows/release.yml. Pushing a tag v0.X.Y builds binaries for x86_64/aarch64 Linux (musl), x86_64/aarch64 macOS and x86_64 Windows, creates the GitHub Release with tarballs, a shell installer and a Homebrew formula pushed to the example/homebrew-tap repo. Version bumps are done with `cargo release minor --execute --no-publish` (cargo-release), which edits all workspace Cargo.toml files and CHANGELOG.md and tags.

Crates are not published to crates.io yet because ferrosync-core's API is unstable; publish = false in all crates. Before tagging: run `cargo dist plan` to see the artifact list, and `cargo test --workspace --all-features` including the MinIO integration tests. The macOS binaries are not notarized; the README tells users to run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine or install via Homebrew.

Recorded points are stored in SQLite via op-sqlite (JSI) rather than MMKV or AsyncStorage, because a 6-hour hike at 1 point/2s is ~11k rows and needs append without rewriting a blob. Schema in src/db/schema.ts: hikes(id, started_at, status), points(hike_id, seq, lat, lon, alt, acc, ts). Migrations are a simple user_version switch.

Some customers could not log in after browsing: Werkzeug warned "The 'session' cookie is too large: the value was 4412 bytes but the header required 26 extra bytes" and browsers dropped the cookie. We had been storing recently used coupon codes and the cart contents in the signed cookie session. Fix: the session now only holds customer id, cart_id and csrf token; cart data lives in carts/cart_items and the Redis cart cache. Rule: nothing list-like goes into flask.session.

Postgres backups (managed by infra on RDS): automated backups with point-in-time recovery for 14 days plus the AWS Backup plan prod-daily with 35-day retention. Restore drill done 2026-10-05: PITR of the 180GB prod DB into a scratch instance took 47 minutes. The anonymized snapshot used by `make snapshot` is a separate nightly pg_dump of the staging-anonymized database, not the prod backup.

Airflow connections: snowflake_default (Snowflake key-pair auth, private key from the airflow-secrets Kubernetes Secret, user SVC_AIRFLOW, role TRANSFORMER), postgres_shopfront_ro and postgres_billing_ro (read replicas). Connections are defined via AIRFLOW_CONN_* env vars from External Secrets, not in the metadata DB, so they are reproducible.

`fsync pull` restores unix permission bits from x-amz-meta-fsync-mode only with --preserve-mode; by default new files get 0644 & !umask. Ownership is never restored. On Windows the mode metadata is ignored.

Redis 7 database numbers in shopfront: 0 = Celery broker, 1 = cache (sf:* keys), 2 = Flask-Limiter, 3 = redbeat scheduler, 4 = locks (fulfillment:export:lock etc.). Do not FLUSHDB on 0 or 3 in staging; flushing 1 is safe because of versioned cache keys.

storage_class per profile (STANDARD, STANDARD_IA, INTELLIGENT_TIERING, GLACIER_IR); files smaller than 128 KiB are always uploaded as STANDARD even when IA is configured because IA bills a 128 KiB minimum. `fsync pull` of GLACIER (not IR) objects is unsupported and reports "object requires restore".

Flask-Limiter uses Redis storage (RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI=redis://redis:6379/2). Limits: POST /login 5/minute per IP and 20/hour per email, POST /api/v1/auth/token 10/minute, POST /checkout/confirm 10/minute per customer. Behind the ingress, key_func reads X-Forwarded-For via ProxyFix(x_for=1).

Cancelling an order (admin or customer before packed) goes through app/services/orders.py:cancel_order: transitions state, releases inventory_reservations or restocks inventory if already committed, cancels the uncaptured PaymentIntent (stripe.PaymentIntent.cancel) and enqueues send_order_cancelled. Never cancel a captured payment; refund it instead.

`fsync pull` writes downloads to name.fsync-tmp-<random> in the same directory, fsyncs, then renames over the target (std::fs::rename, atomic on the same filesystem; on Windows uses MoveFileExW with MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING via the tempfile crate's persist). mtime is set from the x-amz-meta-fsync-mtime metadata with filetime so the next push does not rehash.

Upgrading dbt-core 1.7 -> 1.8 broke tests with "Compilation Error: 'dbt_utils' is undefined" in some singular tests and warnings about tests: being renamed to data_tests:. Fix: `dbt deps` with dbt_utils 1.2.0 (packages.yml), rename tests: to data_tests: in YAML, and install dbt-snowflake 1.8 which now pulls dbt-adapters separately.

User prefers table-driven unit tests using rstest for diff/plan logic and proptest for anything that splits or merges byte ranges. Snapshot tests of CLI output use insta (cargo insta review); do not hand-edit .snap files.

After editing assets/email/order_confirmation.mjml the email still looked old: the compiled HTML in app/templates/email is committed and was not rebuilt. Run `npm run build:email` (mjml 4.15) and commit both files. A pre-commit hook now fails if an .mjml file is newer than its compiled .html.

Payments use Stripe PaymentIntents with automatic_payment_methods and capture_method=manual: we authorize at checkout and capture in the fulfillment task when Kestrel confirms the parcel is packed. Chosen over immediate capture because ~3% of orders are cancelled for stock issues and refunding captured charges cost fees. Authorizations expire after 7 days; a beat task flags orders older than 6 days.

`fsync doctor` checks: config parse, credential resolution (prints which provider in the chain was used), bucket reachability (HeadBucket), clock skew vs the S3 Date header (warns over 60s; RequestTimeTooSkewed otherwise), manifest integrity (PRAGMA integrity_check), NFD keys (--fix-nfd), and stale multipart uploads.

Running two fsync processes on the same root produced "database is locked (code 5: SQLITE_BUSY)" in the second one, sometimes after it had already uploaded files. Fix: an exclusive lock file .ferrosync/lock taken with fs2::FileExt::try_lock_exclusive at startup; the second process now exits immediately with "another fsync run holds the lock (pid 4242)". busy_timeout is also set to 5s for read-only commands like fsync status.

dbt tasks in the KubernetesExecutor were OOMKilled (exit code 137) on fct_order_items compile. The default pod_template gave 512Mi. dbt compile of the full project loads the manifest; Cosmos per-model tasks each load it too. Fix: executor_config pod_override with 2Gi memory for Cosmos tasks via operator_args in DbtTaskGroup, and partial parsing enabled by shipping target/partial_parse.msgpack in the image.

Search autocomplete (GET /search/suggest?q=) uses pg_trgm similarity on products.name with a GIN index ix_products_name_trgm (gin_trgm_ops), threshold set per query with SET LOCAL pg_trgm.similarity_threshold = 0.25, limit 8. Full results still use the tsvector search; trigram is only for the dropdown.

Uploads with SSE-KMS failed only for multipart files with "AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: kms:GenerateDataKey". Single PUT worked because the user's policy allowed kms:Encrypt only via a bucket key. Multipart uploads need kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt (for UploadPart/Complete). Documented the minimal IAM policy in docs/iam-policy.json.

Support users got 403 when refunding 100.00 EUR exactly because the check was amount_cents < 10000. Policy says "up to 100 EUR" inclusive, fixed to <= in app/admin/auth.py:can_refund and added parametrized tests for 9999/10000/10001.

As of 2026-11-15: 3-D Secure support is in progress. Proto has Authorize returning next_action { redirect_url } when the acquirer requires a challenge (status requires_action, new state between authorizing and authorized); the ResumeAuthorization RPC and the acquirer callback endpoint are not implemented yet. Branch feat/3ds; design doc docs/adr/0007-3ds.md.

Scan performance baseline (2026-09, M2 Pro, APFS, 412k files / 380 GB photo library): cold scan with hashing 4m10s, warm scan with unchanged manifest 6.8s (only stat calls). The walk uses ignore's parallel WalkBuilder::build_parallel with 8 threads; the manifest lookup is a prepared statement per file inside one read transaction.

Buttons injected by HTMX partials rendered unstyled in production but fine in dev: Tailwind's content scan did not include app/templates/**/_partials and the classes were built in Python (f"bg-{color}-600"). Fix: add the partials glob to tailwind.config.js content and a safelist pattern /bg-(red|green|amber)-600/; avoid building class names dynamically.

Hashing big files inside async tasks stalled all transfers: tokio worker threads were blocked by blake3 hashing and uploads timed out with "dispatch failure: timeout: error trying to connect: HTTP connect timeout occurred after 3.1s". Fix: hashing runs in tokio::task::spawn_blocking with its own bounded queue (num_cpus permits), and the scan phase finishes hashing before the upload phase starts for files under 1 GiB.

Progress bars flickered and duplicated lines when tracing logs were printed during a run. Fix: route tracing output through MultiProgress::println via a custom MakeWriter (crates/ferrosync-cli/src/output.rs: IndicatifWriter), so log lines are inserted above the bars instead of overwriting them.

Recorded tracks are cleaned before upload in src/features/record/cleanTrack.ts: drop points with horizontalAccuracy > 35 m, drop points implying speed > 12 m/s between consecutive fixes, then Douglas-Peucker simplification with tolerance 3 m (simplify-js). Elevation gain is computed from DEM lookup on the server, not from GPS altitude.

Web runs Gunicorn with 4 sync workers x 2 threads (gthread) per pod, timeout 30, max_requests 2000 with jitter 200. Tried gevent in June; psycopg 3 plus SQLAlchemy pool under gevent caused random "SSL SYSCALL error: EOF detected" under load, so we went back to gthread. Config lives in deploy/gunicorn.conf.py.

Secrets come from AWS Secrets Manager via External Secrets Operator (ClusterSecretStore aws-secrets-manager using IRSA). Chose ESO over Sealed Secrets because secrets are rotated in Secrets Manager by other teams and sealed secrets in git would need a re-seal on every rotation. ExternalSecret refreshInterval is 1h; pods do not reload automatically, so apps that need hot rotation use Stakater Reloader annotations.

Outbox lag alert fired (outbox_oldest_age_seconds > 60). The relay was stuck: "kgo: unable to dial: dial tcp 10.0.4.12:9092: i/o timeout" after the Kafka broker IPs changed, and franz-go only used the seed list resolved at startup. Fix: seed brokers use the bootstrap DNS name kafka-bootstrap.kafka.svc:9092 and the relay's readiness probe fails when no publish succeeded for 2 minutes so Kubernetes restarts it.
